In YouTube Kids a parent's block hides a video only on that child's profile, while a report goes to a 24/7 review queue and, if upheld, removes the video for every user, so one misleading thumbnail can cost a song the whole app.

In the same study channels posting about 5 Shorts a month averaged 8,789 views per long video against 4,364 for channels with no Shorts, but the lift disappeared at 35 or more Shorts a month, a hint (correlation only) that each Short should point clearly to its full song rather than flooding the feed.

Video length beat every thumbnail factor in Eden's data: 41.1% of videos over 40 minutes broke out against 26.9% under 5 minutes, which supports pairing each 2 to 3 minute song with long themed compilations of 30 minutes or more.

A 3M+ subscriber kids channel (Q3 to Q4 2025) gave its near identical uploads, such as a normal and an acoustic version of one song, clearly different visuals with no shared sequences to avoid duplicate content risk, alongside the compilation change that lifted its views 27%.

Another kids channel replaced exaggerated or negative emotion thumbnails with calm, positive, colourful and accurate ones and fixed technical issues through a YouTube review: Browse traffic grew from 6.4M to 17.7M views a quarter (+173%), Suggested from 58M to 75M, total views +41% and revenue +59%.

In the same data a wholesome rural creator's Shorts average about 71,000 views while her long video median is 840, which the analysts read as audiences snacking on the Shorts feed rather than following a person, so Shorts views alone will not build a song channel's loyal audience without long songs and playlists.

YouTube Kids search results are chosen by algorithm without human review and can include recommendations from the child's past viewing; a parent can switch search off, which limits that child to channels verified by YouTube Kids, so being a verified, trusted channel matters for families who lock search.

Children can search YouTube Kids by voice on phones and on TVs, so song titles should start with words a 3 to 6 year old can say clearly ('Dino Stomp', 'Bath Bubbles') rather than invented spellings or long phrases.

Spotter's analysis found Related Shorts links lift long video views by 10% or more, up to 20% when the Short's title and theme closely match the linked video, and Shorts posted within 3 days of the long upload drive the most, since Shorts get most views in their first 7 days.

Because weekend activity in Metricool's model is about half of weekdays on both YouTube and Instagram, our weekly 25 to 45 minute compilation is best released on a weekday (Friday 10 AM fits) and weekends kept for the strongest single songs rather than tests.

YouTube said on 1 Oct 2026 it is cutting Shorts feed reach for channels that mainly re upload content without adding anything of their own, judged at channel level, and that minor technical or template based edits do not make a clip original, so every Bro Bros Short must be a fresh cut with its own hook, not a resized copy.

Todd Beaupre (Creator Insider, Sep 2026) said subscribers click about 10% or less of the uploads shown to them, one viewer was shown a creator's uploads 19 times without noticing, and YouTube has tested capping a video at about eight impressions per viewer, so with 14 songs a week most subscribers miss most songs and each title and thumbnail must win on its own.

Beaupre also advised not benchmarking every upload against the channel's best hit and noted some evergreen videos gain most of their audience a month or more after publishing, so a kids song should be judged on 28 day data, not its first two days.

Creator data gathered by Joos (Dec 2025, unverified) suggests the Home feed now shows as few as two long form videos per row with the next row mostly Shorts, roughly two long to five Shorts on desktop, cutting long form Home slots by up to 80% while Shorts views from Browse rose across 1,000+ channels.

Google said at Made on YouTube (23 Sep 2026) that over 300M users engage with text Posts daily and the Shorts feed will begin recommending Posts, but made for kids channels like ours cannot post them, so this new path helps family vlog rivals, not us.

In AIR's study of 18,000 English channels (Mar 2025 to Mar 2026), small kids channels with 100K to 1M monthly views that post only long form had about 63% more median subscribers (60,100 vs 36,750) than those mixing in Shorts, while at 10M+ monthly views the two groups were equal, so for a young kids channel long songs must stay the core.

The same AIR study puts the best mix at about 25 to 40% Shorts by upload count (kids channels that mix average about 37%), says long form performance falls once Shorts pass about 55% of uploads, and advises shifting the mix gradually over two to three quarters.

Since YouTube's Q1 2026 TV update (14 May 2026) supervised child and teen profiles appear on the TV 'Who's Watching' screen, so more kids watch on the living room TV inside their own supervised profile, where recommendations follow that child's history rather than the parents'.

The same TV update added 'Up Next' teasers at the end of videos to ease the move into the next one, so the last seconds of a Bro Bros song should tease another Bro Bros song (a brother waving 'next, the Wiggle Bus!') rather than end on a blank card, since end screens are off for made for kids videos.

Todd Beaupre (YouTube growth and discovery, Sep 2026) says the Suggested list beside and after a video is the biggest source of views even from a channel's own subscribers, far ahead of the subscriptions feed, so each Bro Bros song should end in a way that flows into our next song and sit in themed playlists.
leaves.src: Creator Insider via PPC Land, Sep 2026

leaves.t: Beaupre also says a brand new channel with no viewer history reaches people mainly through topic matching, so while we are small each song's title, description, first lines and visuals should all state the same single clear topic (brushing teeth, snow day) that families search and watch.
leaves.src: Creator Insider via PPC Land, Sep 2026

leaves.t: The YouTube Kids app has a Your Stuff tab with a Watch it Again row (plus shared and downloaded videos) and topic categories like learning and music on Home, so songs a child replays keep coming back to the top of that child's app; replay value is a direct discovery lever on YouTube Kids.

A 15.8M subscriber kids channel (Heidi dan Zidane) running four to five 24/7 streams of its old hits got 41.9% of its watch time (11.6M hours) and 34.5% of partner revenue from streams, with under one fifth of views, so once we have 30+ songs a nonstop Bro Bros stream is the cheapest way to turn the back catalogue into watch time.

In the same case, stream revenue per view was about 66% higher than regular uploads and streams stay on the YouTube Live shelf, so several themed streams (bedtime, dance party, learning) running at once act like small TV channels for different moods and time zones.

Since August 2026 long YouTube videos can carry localised thumbnails that switch to the viewer's language setting, so a Bro Bros song can show 'Snow Dance!' to English viewers and the same picture with Spanish or Portuguese words to those viewers without new uploads.

AIR's month by month log of YouTube changes (updated 4 Nov 2026) lists no new ranking change in November so far; the last feed changes were the Shorts originality cut on 1 Oct and custom Home feeds on 22 Oct, so our strategy does not need to change this week.

Little Dot Studios (800+ channels, 11.2B monthly views) found that in 2023 and 2024 videos over two hours took a huge share of watch time and revenue, with a 120 minute video earning on average about 100 times a 20 minute one, partly from Premium viewers who avoid ad breaks.

After a significant YouTube algorithm update in January 2025, Little Dot saw ultra long (2 hour plus) viewing fall more than 90% from its 2024 average within three months and the average length of recommended videos halve from about 80 to 40 minutes.

By 2025 Little Dot found average views per video had levelled out across short, long and ultra long formats, and the most popular videos' average length fell 21% (about 35 to 28 minutes) from Dec 2024 to May 2025, so 20 to 40 minute compilations match what YouTube now recommends.

YouTube's video A/B test (shown 23 to 25 Sep 2026) lets a creator upload up to three cuts of the same video, for example different first seconds, and compare their retention curves; unlike title and thumbnail tests it appears the creator, not the system, picks the winner.

No launch date was given for video cut tests, but title testing went live 84 days after its 2025 announcement, which points to roughly mid December 2026 if YouTube follows the same pace; eligibility and made for kids access are not confirmed, and made for kids channels already lose some Studio tools.

YouTube's coming 'dynamic thumbnails' will keep up to three creator chosen thumbnails live at once and show each to the viewer groups it suits best, instead of crowning one winner, which could let one Bro Bros song show a baby friendly image to some viewers and a dance image to others.

The YouTube Kids home organises videos into five curated shelves (series, music, learning, discovery, games), and new users get no personalised recommendations until they have viewing history, so a Bro Bros song should clearly signal music plus one learning point in title and description to land on two shelves.
leaves.src: YouTube Help FAQ via PPC Land, Apr 2026

leaves.t: In YouTube Kids, recommendations are fully automated, an upheld parent report removes a video for all users, and filters are updated quickly when an unsuitable trend appears on main YouTube, so Bro Bros trend videos must not carry trend words or looks that filters may block (zombie, scary, prank) in titles or thumbnails.
leaves.src: YouTube Help FAQ via PPC Land, Apr 2026

leaves.t: Todd Beaupre (Creator Insider, 1 Sep 2026) said some videos peak on their first day while others keep finding audiences for a month or more, so a song with a slow start should be left alone for several weeks rather than deleted or re uploaded.

AIR's month by month tracker of 2026 YouTube changes lists no kids specific ranking change in September or October 2026; the confirmed changes that touch us are Shorts originality (1 Oct), custom Home feeds (22 Oct) and parents' Shorts timers (Jan and Apr 2026).

YouTube's 1 Oct 2026 originality guidance for Shorts says minor technical edits, templates or a voice over that just describes the on screen action do not count as adding value; original storytelling, commentary or distinctive editing does, so Bro Bros compilations and recut Shorts should each add a new hook, scene or caption idea.

Channels downranked in the Shorts feed for mostly reposting get no email, strike or status screen, so a sudden fall in Shorts views is the only sign; keeping every Short visibly new protects the whole channel.
Meta reported that 75% of US Instagram recommendations came from original posts in Q4 2025, a sign that both apps now reward the account that first made a clip over reposters.

The UK government consulted until 31 Aug 2026 on rules that could make YouTube promote public service broadcaster channels (BBC, ITV and others) more visibly, which, if adopted, could add more CBeebies style competition in UK recommendations.

In AIR's study of 31,852 long videos (2025 uploads, 301 channels), Kids and Teens was the most timing sensitive niche: Friday uploads had the best median views (about 36K) and Wednesday the worst, a 379% gap, with the strongest hour at 16:00 UTC and a second peak at 23:00 UTC.

16:00 UTC is 21:30 IST, while Bro Bros posts at 10:00 IST (04:30 UTC) and 16:00 IST (10:30 UTC), times that suit India and Europe but fall before most American families wake, so testing the weekly long compilation at about 21:30 IST on Fridays is worth one experiment.

The same study found 10 to 20 minutes the ideal length band for kids and teens long form and weekdays about 8% better than weekends, while music single tracks of 3 to 10 minutes held about 50% retention.

Metricool's 2026 study found 83% of a video's interactions arrive in its first 10 days and only 11% of channels under 10K subscribers moved up a size tier in a year, so early packaging matters and growth for a new kids channel is normally gradual.

Ask YouTube, the conversational AI search launched in 2026, is open only to signed in US users aged 13 and over and excludes supervised accounts and signed out viewers (confirmed 6 Jul 2026); YouTube says classic search stays, so for kids content keyword titles, descriptions and chapters remain the way searches find us.

YouTube's discovery lead said (Sep 2026) the team tested capping how many times one video is recommended to the same viewer at about eight, after finding an upload recommended 19 times to someone who never noticed it, so a thumbnail and title that fail to earn a click keep wasting impressions and should be refreshed.
leaves.src: Creator Insider via PPC Land, Sep 2026

leaves.t: YouTube advises creators not to judge new uploads against their single best video, because new content can take time to find its audience and each viewer's ranking differs; for us that means judging each song after two to four weeks, not on day one.
leaves.src: Creator Insider via PPC Land, Sep 2026

leaves.t: Since 22 Oct 2026 the US mobile app has a four item bottom bar (Home, Shorts, Create, You) and a 'Subs' tab in the Home top bar beside Live, Music and custom feeds; custom feeds work only for signed in English speakers in the US with history on, so most families abroad still see the classic Home.

No Instagram Reels ranking change was confirmed between August and mid November 2026; the order remains watch time and completion first, then sends per reach, then likes per reach, so our Reels should keep optimising for full watches and shares between parents.

YouTube said on 1 Oct 2026 ('Prioritizing original content on Shorts') that the Shorts feed will give original videos more priority and reduce distribution for channels that mainly re upload others' clips without adding anything; it is judged for the whole channel with no notice, so Bro Bros must never pad the Shorts shelf with other creators' clips, and our own originals gain.

Since April 2026 viewers can set their daily Shorts limit to 0 minutes, which removes the Shorts tab, the Home Shorts shelf and Shorts in Search and Suggested on all their devices; some Shorts only channels saw a 7 to 14% impressions dip in the first week, so our long songs and compilations protect reach among parents who switch Shorts off.

Todd Beaupre (Creator Insider, Sep 2026) said early performance is learned separately for subscribers and for new viewers, so a video can do poorly with subscribers yet still spread to new audiences, most viewing of subscribed channels happens in the Suggested list rather than the Subscriptions feed, and a video should not be judged in its first hour because some peak much later.

Beaupre also advised using separate channels when audiences expect different things and not treating a channel's best video as the benchmark, which supports keeping Hindi stories and English songs on separate Bro Bros channels and judging each song against our median, not our top hit.

Connected TVs carried over 44% of US YouTube watch time in 2026 (about 41% in 2022) and YouTube is 12.5% of all US TV viewing, so our long songs and compilations are mostly judged on the living room screen, where thumbnails, big readable titles and clean audio matter most.

YouTube job listings (Apr 2026) describe 'Stations', 24/7 linear streams on TV, and a 'TV Companion' that lets viewers interact from their phones; these are plans rather than launches, but they point the same way as our 24/7 song stream idea.

In YouTube Kids, recommendations come only from the filtered pool and a brand new child profile is shown editorially curated picks from categories such as series, music, learning, discovery and games until it builds viewing history, so early Bro Bros fans on the Kids app arrive through the curated music shelf and search before personal recommendations kick in.

Team YouTube's YouTube Kids FAQ (1 Apr 2026) says separate automated filters check the thumbnail, the title and the video itself and each one can block a video on its own, so a single scary or busy thumbnail can keep an otherwise perfect song out of the YouTube Kids app.
leaves.src: PPC Land citing YouTube Help, Apr 2026

leaves.t: Todd Beaupre (Creator Insider, 1 Sep 2026) said Suggested videos, not the subscriptions feed, are the number one place viewers watch channels they subscribe to, so each Bro Bros song should sit naturally next to our other songs and the big rhyme hits on the same topic.

For a new channel with no viewer history YouTube matches the video's topic to viewers likely to enjoy it, and if no interested group shows up, impressions simply stop, so a clear single topic in each title, thumbnail and opening helps a new song find its first audience.

YouTube stopped sending push notifications to inactive subscribers in April 2026, and one channel with about 21,900 subscribers saw only seven notifications go out for an upload; made for kids videos get no bell notifications anyway, so our reach depends on recommendations, not alerts.

SocialBee's running log of YouTube changes (updated 9 Nov 2026) lists no Home or recommendation change for late October or November; YouTube is instead building a tool to help viewers manage watching across all formats, not only Shorts, which could shorten family viewing sessions later.

A kids channel that dropped re uploads and repetitive food videos for original story led videos in 4K, paced for TV viewing, and added 4K live streams with mid rolls and vertical shorts grew views 55% (3.6M to 5.7M) and revenue 77%, supporting originality and TV friendly quality as growth levers.

Buffer's study of about 1.8M videos (Jul 2026) found long videos get the most engagement on Sunday about 10 AM local time (and Monday, Tuesday mornings), while Shorts peak on Friday, Saturday and Thursday evenings from about 6 to 11 PM, with Monday and Tuesday weakest; kids content was not separated, so test against our own data.

In Buffer's data the best and worst long video slots differ hugely (engagement factor 0.95 on Sunday 10 AM against 0.11 on Thursday 2 PM), and the times are local to each viewer; our 10 AM IST slot lands at about 5:30 AM in Central Europe and late evening in the US, and 4 PM IST at late morning in Europe and early morning in the US, so one weekend morning upload timed for Europe or the Americas is worth testing.

In YouTube Kids, 'Approve content yourself' limits a child to videos, channels and collections a parent picks; collections are topic groups (such as music or science) chosen by the YouTube Kids team or partners, so being included in a YouTube Kids music collection is one of the few ways into the strictest households.

YouTube Kids parents can pause watch history (new views stop shaping Recommended and Watch it again), pause search history and switch off autoplay separately, so in some homes our next song only plays if the child taps it, another reason for bright, readable thumbnails of one clear character.

Parents choose a YouTube Kids level (Preschool, Younger, Older or approve it themselves) in the app or in Family Link, and the self approval mode can only be switched on inside the YouTube Kids app, so a parent facing Instagram caption like 'find us in YouTube Kids, search Bro Bros' helps families add us by hand.

YouTube states that applying an AI label by itself does not affect recommendations or monetisation eligibility, so ticking the altered content box when it truly applies costs no reach; what hurts is low quality or template content, not the label.

Since about April 2026 the YouTube app sometimes opens straight into the Shorts player instead of Home, even for people who rarely watch Shorts, which makes the first second of every Short (a face, movement and sound at once) count even more, since many Shorts views now start without the viewer choosing them.

YouTube is rolling out Live Practice Mode in the mobile app (by Oct 2026), a private rehearsal space for live streams, so a looping Bro Bros Christmas stream can be tested for sound levels, overlays and loop gaps before it goes public in December.

AIR's tracker lists no new confirmed YouTube recommendation change after the 1 Oct 2026 Shorts originality update up to 4 Nov 2026, so current priorities stay the same: original Shorts, satisfying first 30 seconds and consistent uploads, rather than chasing a rumoured update.

YouTube Kids has no personal history for a new child profile, so it starts from editorial picks and the filtered catalogue; channels that already earn repeat viewing on main YouTube are the ones that surface first when a new Kids profile begins watching.

A 24/7 kids stream checklist (Gyre, updated Nov 2026): made for kids on, chat, comments and notifications off, no outbound links, only copyright safe music, every file checked by hand, clean non clickbait thumbnails, a title that matches what is actually playing (a mismatch can be flagged) and playlists rotated with mixed clip lengths so the loop does not look repetitive.

A Korean kids and teens channel (3.92M subscribers) that added automated 24/7 streams grew revenue about 80% and watch time about four times in 90 days, more evidence that looping streams of existing songs are the cheapest big lever for a song catalogue.

A 731K subscriber DIY channel ran four themed 24/7 streams at once from existing videos and average view duration rose from 1:56 on uploads to 5:58 inside the streams, with streams reaching about 15% of income; for us four themed loops (Christmas, bedtime, dance party, animals) would let each stream match a different parent need.

Even a small entertainment channel that rebroadcast its old videos as 24/7 streams grew stream views from about 65K to 800K and stream watch time about 13 fold in six months (Jan to Jun 2025), so streaming helps channels of our size too, not only giants.

YouTube's Todd Beaupré said most videos, even a channel's best, get about a 10% or lower click rate in the Subscriptions row, so subscribers ignoring most uploads is normal and not a penalty; the watch page Suggested list matters far more.

YouTube has tested capping repeat recommendations of the same video to one viewer at about eight times (one upload was shown 19 times to a viewer who never noticed it), so a song that is ignored keeps a few more chances but not endless ones; a fresh thumbnail or a new Short is the way to reopen it.

At Made on YouTube (Sep 2026) YouTube said over 600M logged in viewers watched live content daily in August and more than 40% of live watch time comes from outside a creator's home country, so a 24/7 Bro Bros song stream should be planned for a worldwide audience across time zones.

Channels that combine Shorts with long form videos grow about 41% faster than channels using only one format (aggregated industry data), which supports our mix of full songs, weekly compilations and two or more Shorts per song.

A million subscriber kids song channel turned most of its 2 to 3 minute songs into compilations of about 10 minutes in Q4 2025: those compilations gained about 19% watch duration, 9% higher CPM and 72% higher RPM, and total views rose 27% (355M to 450M a quarter) with several Shorts a day added.

The same channel gave every alternate version of a song (for example an acoustic version) its own distinct visuals and never reused identical video sequences, to avoid duplicate content signals; our slow or Spanish versions of a hit should get new scenes, not the same render with new audio.

A kids channel that went from one manual live stream to 16 automated 24/7 streams, posted 13 long videos instead of 9 and started Shorts cut from its liveliest moments raised average view duration from 1:36 to 2:06 (+31% watch time) and revenue 63% while views rose only 13% (Q4 2025).

Socialinsider advises keeping Shorts and long videos separate in analytics, because channel averages hide strong or weak Shorts; for Bro Bros this means a weekly check of Shorts by themselves (views, swipe away rate) next to a separate check of full songs.

vidIQ's upload frequency study of 10.2M channels with 1,000+ subscribers (Apr 2025 to Mar 2026) found median monthly view growth of 0.53% for under 1 upload a month, 0.89% for 1 to 3, 1.32% for 4 to 7, 1.70% for 8 to 11 and 2.18% for 12 or more, and subscriber growth rising from 0% to 0.91%; frequency correlates with growth, though healthier channels may simply post more.

OverseerOS measured 2,543 upload gaps on 53 channels (Aug 2026) and found the time since the previous upload made no clear difference to a video's chance of breaking out (about 9.5% to 12% in every gap band), so posting often does not tire out the audience or hurt each new song's chance, and a short pause does not reset a channel.

Taken together, the two 2026 frequency studies suggest Bro Bros' 14 songs a week helps channel level growth as long as each song stays distinct and well made, since breakout odds per video do not depend on cadence; quality per upload, not the gap between uploads, decides each song's reach.

Since YouTube's May 2026 TV update its conversational AI can be called with the remote's microphone to answer questions about the video that is playing without stopping it, another reason for clear chapters and plain descriptions that say what each song teaches and when.

In the Vania Mania kids network, adding a Portuguese dub as an extra audio track on already successful videos (rather than new uploads) brought nearly 5M extra views in about six months, so our best English songs should get a Portuguese and Spanish audio track first.

The same network's French channel grew Suggested traffic 42% (21.2M to 30.1M a quarter), views 37% and revenue 60% in Q4 2025 after warm, single focus thumbnails, hook first titles and one change at a time to old videos' metadata.

AIR advises uploading the highest quality master file possible (it mentions files up to 256GB) because YouTube's TV placement favours sharp, high bitrate video, so we should export our Blender renders at the best quality and not upload compressed copies.

Vania Mania's live channel went from 3.1M to 11.4M views in a quarter as Suggested traffic rose 351% while uploads grew only from 32 to 42, showing that live and looping streams are mainly fed by Suggested, not search or subscribers.

A Spanish kids channel that YouTube deleted, most likely an automated false positive, stayed deleted after a rejected appeal but was restored with all its history and standing once its agency documented the cause and escalated to YouTube partner contacts, so a rejected appeal is not the end; keep clean records of our original songs and production files for such a case.

The same partner's Arabic kids channel grew from about 253M to 437M views a quarter (+72%) and revenue 133% in Q4 2025 after daily checks of every upload and thumbnail, pacing and metadata changes aligned with YouTube's kids quality principles, which suggests small compliance problems quietly throttle Suggested and Shorts reach with no strike or warning.

YouTube plans an Ask Studio tool that suggests refreshed thumbnails for older videos (global rollout planned for early 2027), useful for reviving our back catalogue of songs without re rendering, as long as each new thumbnail is still checked by hand for kids quality.

YouTube also announced audience specific thumbnails, up to 3 images each shown to a different viewer group (no date given), which would let one Bro Bros song show, for example, a calm face to bedtime viewers and a dance pose to party viewers; no kids or family features were announced at Made on YouTube 2026.

In an AIR case (Sep 2024 to Aug 2025) a mid sized European channel added AI translated, human edited subtitles in 20+ languages plus translated titles, descriptions and tags (Spanish, Hindi, Portuguese, Turkish, Vietnamese) to videos showing early promise; views rose 10.7%, subtitled videos produced about 22% of all views and translated metadata about 8%, so translating titles and descriptions is a cheap first localisation step before full dubbing.

For a song channel whose viewers are too young to read, translated titles and descriptions matter more than subtitles, because they let parents find the video in YouTube search and Suggested in their own language, while on screen lyrics stay a bonus for older children.

Creator benchmarks say a Short whose average view lasts over 80% of its length travels beyond subscribers while below 60% it stalls; for a 30 second Short that means at least 24 seconds watched on average (these are creator figures, not YouTube's).

Creator data suggests per Short retention tends to drop when a channel posts more than about 7 Shorts a week, so with 14 songs a week Bro Bros should keep Shorts to the best cut of each song and spread them, rather than adding many extra Shorts per song.

Meta added a 'User True Interest Survey' model to Facebook Reels ranking: random in feed polls ask 'How well does this video match your interests?' on a five point scale, and in a 10M user test videos that match viewers' real interests got modest boosts while poor matches were demoted; Meta has not said it runs on Instagram, but it rewards a channel that stays clearly on one topic (kids songs).

vidIQ's study of 32.9M channels under 1,000 subscribers (Sep 2026) found that within a year 30.8% of channels adding 52 or more videos reached 1,000 subscribers, against 8.65% for 12 to 51 videos, 1.86% for 1 to 11 and 0.2% for none; it is a pattern, not proof, but steady volume clearly matters and our 14 songs a week already clears it, so quality and hooks, not volume, are our lever.
Cocomelon is still the biggest kids channel (about 200M subs, about 229B views); its top video is Wheels on the Bus (8.4B).
Baby Shark Dance (Pinkfong) is the most-viewed YouTube video ever, about 17.5B views (Nov 2026).
Next tier: ChuChu TV (about 98M), Super Simple Songs, Infobells Hindi (about 73M), Vlad and Niki, Kids Diana Show, Like Nastya.
Ms. Rachel (live, slow, speech-focused) became a top-4 Netflix kids show in her first year; creator-led preschool content is rising.
Multi-language dubbing is a key growth lever for the biggest kids channels (Diana, Nastya, ChuChu's 12 language channels).
Long compilations and 24/7 live streams of the back catalogue keep old songs earning views.
Cocomelon's biggest buckets are fresh spins on classic rhymes and originals that blend a classic with a modern hook; its average video length grew to about 20 minutes (compilations).
Seven of the 10 most-watched YouTube Kids videos of 2019 were songs/nursery rhymes, and the top one was a 36-minute song compilation.
A proven repeatable formula: a familiar song or character placed in a new world or holiday ('X visits the Magic Forest / Christmas'), packaged as sing-along.
Bebefinn (Pinkfong) is about 84M subscribers and 65 billion views brand wide; its Netflix series hit No. 1 kids title in 12 countries and an Amazon Kids+ series is coming.

Bebefinn's main English channel (37M subs) gets about 370M views a month; its top videos are a wake up morning routine (775M), a Baby Shark crossover, a mix compilation and a 'Run Away Baby Car' chase.
Bebefinn's newest uploads are pretend play job stories (car mechanics fixing a car) with emoji led titles and a brand hashtag, posted about 4 to 5 times a week.

Lalafun, a 3D nursery rhyme channel started in Oct 2022, reached 15M subscribers and 11.6 billion views in about 4 years at 3 to 4 uploads a week, now 600 to 700M views a month: a new 3D channel can break through fast.

Lalafun's biggest hits are animal twists on public domain rhymes with a learning tag: Wheels on the Bus Animal Version (955M), 5 Little Ducks Learn Colors (726M), Old MacDonald with Safari Animals, Counting 10 Little Pandas.
Lalafun's latest titles frame a small mystery the song solves ('Where did the animals' colours go?'), turning a colours song into a rescue story.

Bebefinn launched with a crossover starring the company's existing mega hit character, and that episode is still its second most viewed; reusing our own recurring friends across songs builds the same pull.

VocaVoca (US, kids songs, mostly Shorts) hit #23 in Tubefilter's worldwide top 50 with about 527M weekly views; its monthly views rose from about 0.5B in May to 2.9B in Oct 2026 with 1.56M new subscribers that month.

VocaVoca's biggest songs teach healthy habits and safety: going to the dentist (164M), caring for a baby, police officer job song, stranger safety, and a buckle up song in the 'no no, I don't want to' refusal format, plus new good manners cartoons.

In the 8 Nov 2026 Tubefilter top 50, Indian family channels rode Diwali: Baccha Mat Bolna (#28, 415M weekly views) mixes festival vlogs with childhood games like 'the floor is lava', and Paintellectual PriyA (#40) teaches young viewers to draw festive lamps.

ChuChu TV (Chennai, founded 2013) reports 180M+ digital subscribers and 110 billion views and signed a worldwide Netflix deal in Sep 2026 for Surprise Eggs, Drawing with ChuChu, Colors in FunZone and Nursery Rhymes in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.

ChuChu TV is turning a YouTube song channel into a global preschool franchise (licensing, toys, publishing, live shows) through a North American partner, showing an Indian 3D song brand can scale worldwide.
ChuChu TV's Netflix collections are learning formats (colours, drawing, surprise reveals, rhymes), confirming that colour and draw along songs travel across languages.
Cocomelon's main channel is at about 203M subscribers in Nov 2026, still the largest kids channel.

Kids channels in that week's top 50 subscriber gainers: Pokemon Kids TV (#23, about 400K a week), Cadel and Mia (#37, Australian family) and VocaVoca kids songs (#45, about 300K a week, steady for weeks).

Pokemon Kids TV (44.8M subs, about 71M views in 28 days) gets its biggest song hits from short dance songs built around one named character (One Pikachu dance song, 226M; Scorbunny Dancing, 94M), proving a signature character dance is evergreen.

Sasha Show (Russian language) jumped 9.5M subscribers in Oct 2026 with sensational Shorts using famous borrowed characters (Sonic, PAW Patrol, Ladybug) and scary or naughty titles; this is the low quality pattern YouTube's kids principles penalise, so it is not a model for us.

Animaj (owner of Pocoyo) launched Ozzy Fox in Jul 2026 on YouTube and YouTube Kids: each episode centres on one original song that turns an everyday routine into a mission; the first two episodes passed 1.5M views in under five days.

Super Simple Songs (47.3M subs) rose from about 490M monthly views in Jan 2026 to about 590M in Oct 2026 while gaining only 100 to 200K subscribers a month: a deep song library keeps compounding views long after upload.

Super Simple Songs' all time leaders are puppet led action and counting songs (500 Ducks, 214M; If You're Happy and You Know It Spin Around, 176M; Five Little Speckled Frogs, 164M), and its newest release (5 Nov 2026) is a wash your hands and face routine song with about 900K views in 9 days.

A Little Angel channel (about 7.3M subs) posting daily in Oct 2026 got only 7K to 30K views on most play and adventure episodes, while its Brush Your Teeth healthy habit song got 96K, so routine songs beat generic play stories even for a big brand.

On that Little Angel channel the dance Short (Do the Daddy and Jill Dance) drew the most likes of the recent uploads (344 versus under 100 for most long videos), backing family dance moments as Short material.

Mexico's El Tren Nam Nam reached No. 2 among all YouTube channels worldwide in the week of 25 Oct 2026 with about 1.08B weekly views (up 96%), driven by an animated tooth mascot telling kids to brush for two minutes before Halloween.

VocaVoca's most watched Short is a morning routine oral care song uploaded in early September that took off in October; it also uses a tooth mascot, and two of the world's top 11 channels that week rode tooth brushing.

Family Shorts channels Jasmin and James (Germany, about 1.03B weekly views) and Cadel and Mia (Australia, about 0.89B) were No. 3 and No. 5 worldwide in late Oct 2026, and Tiny Splash Academy entered at No. 43.
After Halloween VocaVoca's weekly views fell 22% (to about 527M, from No. 11 to No. 23), showing seasonal topic spikes fade within a week, so holiday songs must post before the peak.

BabyBus (43.9M subs, about 36B views) posts about 5.6 long form videos a week averaging about 31 minutes each; 96% of uploads are long form and 95% evergreen, a compilation heavy model built for TV sessions.
BabyBus's recent breakout was Sharing is Caring 2 (Can You Share? Take Turns), 54M views or 28 times its median, so a sharing and taking turns song is a proven global hit topic.

BabyBus's other recent outliers wrap a lesson inside pretend play adventure: a cardboard box escape room with a brave policeman (26M), baby lost his colours plus mosquitoes go away (16M), chase the dinosaurs to learn colours (14M) and kids turn into superheroes to catch bugs (13M).
BabyBus titles stack the story hook first, then the lesson, then the category: 'Sharing is Caring 2 | Can You Share? | Take Turns | Nursery Rhymes and Kids Songs | BabyBus'.

Koko and Golu (India, 13.8M subs) gained about 2.4B views in Oct 2026, up from about 1.6 to 1.9B a month over the summer, and 700K subs in 28 days, with Hindi titled comedy Shorts about two characters.

Koko and Golu's most viewed long uploads are 'best funniest moments' compilations (12.6M) and live videos, and its newest Short (rescuing a cake, 13 Nov 2026) hit about 9.9M views in 34 hours, so a funny 'save the treat' moment plus a best of compilation is a proven Indian pattern.

Baby Shark has ranked No. 1 in global YouTube views for 71 consecutive months (Oct 2026), and Pinkfong releases a Christmas sing and dance along film on 5 Dec built around a Santa selection contest and a look alike mischief rival.

Pinkfong drops its Christmas album in two stages (10 and 27 Nov, 15 tracks with 7 new songs), so the biggest kids brand starts holiday music by mid November and keeps a second wave for early December.

CoComelon and Headspace's Wiggle to Wind Down runs about 20 minute episodes that start with gentle wiggles and stretches and end in calm stories, after a survey where 45% of 500 US parents named bedtime one of their biggest daily struggles.
VocaVoca's monthly views rose from about 370M in Jan 2026 to 2.91B in Oct 2026 (nearly eight times), with the jump from July onward driven by routine Shorts like its morning oral care song.

VocaVoca's all time long form leaders are still 2021 to 2022 habit and safety songs (Dentist Song 164M, Baby Care 68M, Police Officer job song 52M, stranger safety 42M, seatbelt 37M), so evergreen routine songs keep feeding a channel for years.

VocaVoca titles lead with one or two emojis and the song name, then the benefit ('Healthy Habits for Kids', 'Job and Career Songs for Children'), then the brand with its avocado emoji, a consistent pattern across all its hits.

Dave and Ava (3D nursery rhymes, 15.9M subs, 12.8B views) gained zero subscribers in 2026 and only about 37 to 57M views a month, with its top videos still 2021 to 2022 Halloween and firemen compilations and a new Head Shoulders Knees and Toes upload at about 30K views in two days: a classic rhyme library without fresh formats or Shorts stalls.

Pinkfong's Hogi channel (16.7M subs) earns about 220 to 365M views a month in 2026; its biggest hits teach colours through objects kids crave (Learn Colors with Colorful Pop It 306M, with Candies 138M, Monster Candy Shop 125M), and its newest breakout is Roar! Dino Special (95M, Aug 2025).

Hogi's newest Short (5 Nov 2026) is a 'What's inside the dinosaur egg?' reveal, the same surprise reveal question hook ChuChu TV sells to Netflix as Surprise Eggs; a hatch or unwrap reveal in the first seconds is a proven kids Shorts opener we can do with our own original objects.

In Tubefilter's most viewed chart for the week of 8 Nov 2026 family Shorts channels hold four of the top 11 spots: Cadel and Mia (#3, 890M weekly views), Sierra and Rhia English (#6, 743M), Sierra and Rhia FAM (#8, 705M) and Jasmin and James (#11, 623M); Sierra and Rhia run two near equal channels, one of them English only.
El Tren Nam Nam fell 52% to about 360M weekly views two weeks after its Halloween tooth brushing peak, the second clear case this autumn of a seasonal habit spike fading within about two weeks.

ChuChu TV's main English channel was at 98.2M subscribers and 61B views on 15 Nov 2026 with no subscriber change in 28 days; the brand's growth now comes from Netflix, regional language channels and spin off series rather than the flagship.

ChuChu TV's 30 minute 'Classics: Rain Rain Go Away and many more' compilation has 109M views and still draws about 1,000 views an hour, while a new 19 minute animal songs compilation has about 244K: old compilations of proven songs keep compounding, new mixes start small.

ChuChu TV now pushes story spin offs like ChuChu TV Police (toy squad cartoons teaching safety) with titles built as emoji, cartoon name, story hook and 'Funny Kids Cartoon'; a 4:45 Candy Robbery episode reached about 440K views, far below its song compilations.

Kids Diana Show (138M YouTube subscribers) showed zero YouTube subscriber growth in CreatorDB's Oct 2026 snapshot despite about 5 uploads a week and 0.9% engagement, and its most viewed recent posts are Gulf travel and mall event promos: toy and role play family giants have plateaued.

vidIQ's 30 day subscriber growth list to 14 Nov 2026 is led by Sasha Show (+8.8M) and Brazilian, Spanish speaking and Indian family creators; the kids brands near the top are Pokemon Kids TV (#18, +1.7M) and El Tren Nam Nam (#20, +1.6M), with VocaVoca (#42) the first pure kids song channel.

Kids Funny Songs (US, 7.78M subs, since 2021) saw its counted total views fall from about 6.91B to 5.36B in early November 2026 through large negative daily corrections, a warning that big song libraries can lose views at once after removals or audits.

Kids Funny Songs' newest upload 'Who's in the Egg?' (11 Nov) drew about 55K views in a day and a half, the same egg reveal question hook that Hogi and ChuChu TV use, which keeps proving itself across channels this month.

A year earlier (week of 23 Nov 2025) the kids and family channels in Tubefilter's top 50 were Cadel and Mia (#2, 1.04B weekly), Diary of 4, KIDZOKI, Toys and Colors, Kidshire and Kids Land, with 41 of the 50 mainly Shorts channels, so holiday season kids reach is Shorts led every year.

CoComelon: The Movie (Universal Pictures, with DreamWorks Animation) opens in US cinemas on 19 Feb 2027; JJ starts kindergarten with new songs and friends, so 'first day of school' and 'making new friends' themes will get a publicity wave in January and February 2027.

Pinkfong ended Baby Shark's tenth anniversary with a Baby Shark x Peppa Pig dance remix that blends both theme songs, released on Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music on 26 Dec and as a YouTube video on 29 Dec: audio first, video days later, in the quiet week after Christmas.

Pinkfong also turned the boy from the original Baby Shark Dance video into a K pop singer (debut single 'Wave' in Aug 2026 with MONSTA X's Jooheon), stretching one kids hit into a teen music brand as its first viewers grow up.

The 15 most subscribed kids channels on 4 Nov 2026: CoComelon 203M, Vlad and Niki 151M, Kids Diana Show 138M, ChuChu TV 98.2M, Pinkfong 85.3M, Toys and Colors 83.1M, Infobells Hindi 72.9M, El Reino Infantil 71.6M, LooLoo Kids 62.7M, JioHotstar Kids 58.5M, Billion Surprise Toys 57.6M, Luccas Neto 53.6M, Genevieve's Playhouse 51.2M, Little Baby Bum 41.6M and Ryan's World 40.4M.

Nine of those top 15 are animated song or rhyme brands, and the shared traits are simple repeatable formats with recurring characters, a learning point (counting, colours, morals), bright recognisable visuals and plain keyword titles such as 'nursery rhymes' and 'kids songs'.

Single language giants still reach the top 15 (El Reino Infantil in Spanish, Luccas Neto in Portuguese, Infobells in Hindi), and Billion Surprise Toys grew through Hindi, English, Indonesian, Korean, Spanish and Arabic versions, showing home market depth and wide dubbing both work.

Moonbug's content chief (Jun 2026): stay YouTube first and non exclusive, be on every platform families use, and make content for each viewing moment, from short phone clips on a car journey to longer living room co viewing; hits then extend into Spotify music, toys and live tours.

Moonbug gives a whole year a theme (Blippi's 'Year of Vehicles' in 2026) and spins side characters into their own shows (Emmie's Wonder Wardrobe from Little Angel, for ages 3 to 5), a model for giving each Bro Bros friend a themed month or a mini series.

Moonbug says its next growth push in Europe is Spain and France, and its Little Baby Bum brand ('not about music, it is music') moved to a Netflix series with a new curriculum and a soundtrack on every music service, showing music brands travel from YouTube to streaming with audio alongside.

Danny Go! (5.43M subs, 6.33B views) earns about 170 to 195M views a month from only 131 videos; its newest upload 'Burning ENERGY! Don't Stop Moving Challenge' (9 Sep 2026) reached about 21.5M views in two months, so a few big, rewatchable movement videos can beat a high upload count.

Ms Rachel had 21.5M YouTube subscribers in Oct 2026 (+1.4% in 30 days) but grew 9.4% on Instagram (6.07M) with about 22 posts a week and 6.7% engagement, showing Instagram can grow fast for a kids brand when parents follow the face behind it.

Ms Rachel's most viewed videos are routine and milestone helpers parents search for: a shapes, letters and numbers learning video (287M), potty training (200M), hide and seek with Elmo (152M), friendship and social skills (110M) and a brush your teeth song (106M).

In vidIQ's US trending channels for the 30 days to 14 Nov 2026, VocaVoca (kids songs) was No. 3 overall with about 1.6B views gained, ahead of CoComelon at No. 17 with about 1.08B, so a Shorts led habit song channel now out gains the biggest brand in the US.

Doctor Sophia, a 'Healthy Habits for Kids' channel built around a doctor character, gained about 651M US views in those 30 days, backing our own best performer (Lion Needs a Doctor) and the case for a recurring friendly doctor or helper in our songs.

Nursery rhyme channels keep scaling in the US: Lalafun (+654M views in 30 days), Toddler Zoo (+530M) and NuNu TV (+447M), alongside the bilingual Spanish English family music act 123 Andres (+868M), so both classic rhyme songs and bilingual music have big US demand.

Super Simple Songs reached 20 years in 2026 with over 70M subscribers and over 90B views; it began as teachers writing simple songs to help pupils learn English and now has a self funded Toronto studio of 40+ animators, musicians, puppeteers and educators.

Super Simple Songs now uploads about once a week, alternating a new song with a 'Top 20' themed compilation (counting, circle time, back to school, book songs), and its themed Top 20 mixes earn 1.1 to 3.5M views each, a steady compilation rhythm for a mature channel.

Super Simple's strongest new song of 2026 is an upbeat 'everybody celebrate' party song (6M views in under three months), ahead of a counting to 20 sea animals song made with another kids channel (3.1M) and a pack your bag trip song (2.7M): party, counting and adventure themes lead.

Lalafun (15.2M subs, 714 videos since Oct 2022) gains 600 to 700M views and 500 to 700K subscribers a month from about 15 uploads a month; its all time hits are classic rhymes with a twist: animal version Wheels on the Bus (955M), Five Little Ducks colours (726M), Old MacDonald safari (407M), counting 10 pandas (337M).

Lalafun runs local language channels (German, Indonesian, Arabic, Canada and US feeds), and its newest US video uses a mystery question title ('Where did the animals' colours go?'), the same curiosity hook that works for Shorts.

Super Simple Songs also partners with outside brands and channels for single songs (a hockey song with the NHL, a counting song with Noodle and Pals), a way big kids channels borrow each other's audiences.

Because classroom viewing runs through teachers, songs that work for circle time (a clear learning point, a calm teacher friendly title, no ads style hype) can reach children through lesson plans; Super Simple Songs was built exactly this way by teachers.

Bebefinn, Pinkfong's 3D baby and family song brand launched only in 2022, reported more than 80M subscribers and 58B views across its YouTube channels in Jun 2026 and about 84M and 65B by Aug 2026, the fastest climb of any new 3D kids song brand.

Pinkfong's first Amazon Kids+ original, The Big Book of Bebefinn (announced Jun 2026), is 18 musical episodes of about seven minutes following a toddler through everyday firsts such as riding a tricycle, visiting the doctor and trying new foods, mixing new songs with fan favourite hits.

La Granja de Zenon started in 2011 as preschool farm songs, and its named animal characters (a cow, a little rooster, a horse) grew bigger than the songs, so a small cast of recurring named animal friends around the Bros can become the brand kids ask for.

When CoComelon's main channel matured it grew through side character spin off channels: JJ's Animal Time reached 200M+ views a month (with its own animal songs and adventures spin offs), Cody Time 60M+ and Nina's Familia 40M+, so an animals themed Bro Bros playlist or sub series is the proven next step once the main channel has traction.

Little Angel's main English channel (7.3M subs, 2,278 videos) gained only 0 to 10K subscribers and 14 to 36M views in most months of 2026 (Aug spiked to 125M), so even a Moonbug brand's single channel plateaus without new formats; its Spanish, Portuguese and Indonesian channels carry much of the growth.

123 Andres, a Grammy and Latin Grammy winning bilingual Spanish English family music act, has 13.2M subscribers and 26.9B views from 3,013 videos, and its monthly views climbed from about 448M (Aug 2026) to 583M (Sep) and 797M (Oct), with new uploads reaching about 800K views in a day and a half.

In vidIQ's US ranking (Nov 2026) Toys and Colors has 123B lifetime views on 83M subscribers (about 1,480 views per subscriber) versus about 1,130 for CoComelon, and Filaretiki has about 1,220, so the channels kids replay most are simple, repeatable play formats rather than the biggest subscriber counts.

Pinkfong and Dr Seuss Enterprises made their first crossover on 16 Oct 2026: a Baby Shark Halloween remix plus a 'Guess Baby Shark's Halloween Costume!' sing along where viewers guess each costume, posted on both channels so each brand feeds the other's audience.

Dr Seuss Enterprises' relaunched YouTube channel reached 230.9M views and 2M subscribers in just over two years by turning classic characters into baby versions for nursery style songs, the same baby character trick CoComelon and Bebefinn use.

Disney bought Gracie's Corner, a family made YouTube sing along brand (6.3M subscribers, nearly 10B views) with original songs like a Good Morning Song, Veggie Dance and Play Outside, as a library of 120+ shorts and 18 themed compilations for Disney+ and Disney Jr. from 15 Jun 2026, with new originals to follow.

Disney Jr. itself makes short stop motion sing along music videos for each holiday (Mickey and Minnie's Holiday Songs: Halloween, then Christmas), so seasonal short sing along clips are a format even the biggest studio uses for preschoolers.

Peppa Pig revealed in 2026 that little brother George is moderately deaf (new season from 23 Mar, with short clips first on its YouTube channel), its second disabled character after wheelchair user Mandy Mouse, made with the National Deaf Children's Society and a deaf script consultant; disability is still rare in kids TV, so a natural inclusive friend in Bro Bros would stand out.

LooLoo Kids (62.7M subscribers, 43B views) titles almost every new upload as a medley of its recurring Johny character plus a classic rhyme ('Bath Song + Wheels on the Bus'), and its seasonal Halloween medleys reached 8 to 12M views within weeks in Oct 2026, so naming two familiar songs in one title widens Search reach.

LooLoo Kids' recent uploads cover healthy habits and safety (brushing teeth, bath time, handwashing, bus safety rules) alongside colours, fruits and phonics, showing routine songs are a core, steady earner for top nursery channels.

Hey Bear Sensory has about 3.4B views from only 95 videos (about 35M per video) with dancing fruit and veggie characters on plain black backgrounds and wordless funk, house and disco tracks; its biggest hits are 10 to 27 minute mixes (Smoothie Mix 383M, Fruit Salad Dance Party 334M), while its recent 1 to 5 minute uploads average only about 5M.

CreatorDB's study of 417 surging channels over 500K subscribers (Sep 2026) found 24% post 60+ times a month and 42% at least daily, but median subscribers gained per upload were about 98,800 for channels posting under 8 times a month, 16,100 for regular, 6,100 for heavy and only 1,900 for the heaviest posters: volume buys reach, not loyalty.

CoComelon's Netflix viewing fell 30% in H2 2025 and the brand moves to Disney+ in January 2027, while creator led YouTube shows (Ms Rachel, CrunchLabs) rose, so the market now rewards a warm personality and fresh feel over a polished nursery rhyme factory.

Little Baby Bum (41.6M subscribers, 44.8B views) has had flat or falling subscribers since early 2025 yet still earns about 110 to 140M views a month, proof that an old nursery catalogue lives on recommendations and repeat viewing, not new subscribers.

All five of Little Baby Bum's most viewed videos are Wheels on the Bus variants: Halloween Wheels on the Bus (275M), Ten Little Buses (112M and 69M), Bus Wash (60M) and Wheels on the Bus Underwater (56M), so a single proven song re set in new places and seasons is a repeatable hit engine.

Little Baby Bum's newest Shorts are counting songs with a twist on a known rhyme ('Ten Shiny Stars Roll Out of Bed', 5 Nov 2026), reaching about 53K views in under two days, so classic counting down structures (ten in the bed, five little ducks) adapt well to Shorts.

In Tubefilter's most viewed list for the week of 8 Nov 2026, kid duo and family channels fill the top: Cadel and Mia 890M weekly views (down from first to third), Sierra and Rhia English and Sierra and Rhia FAM both up 7%, Keizo and Friends climbing from 29th to 20th, so sibling and friend pairs are the format kids binge most.

GoBooBoo (4.29M subscribers) gets about 36M views a month from only 197 videos, roughly 180K monthly views per video, and its all time hit Baby Finger Where Are You passed 930M views, so a small catalogue of well made songs can outearn a huge one.

Junior Squad has 1,164 videos and 5.45M subscribers but only about 4.4M views in the last 28 days, and its newest 2 minute rhyme got about 3K views in two days, a warning that high volume rhyme uploads without strong recurring characters stall.

GoBooBoo titles pair an original named song with a known rhyme hook (Boo Boo Song plus Wheels on the Ambulance, 150M) and its second biggest hit is a gentle fear song, Something in the Dark (194M), so mild spooky or brave in the dark themes work for preschoolers.

Stomp! Stomp! Rhinos!, a kids feelings channel that teaches calming down and mindfulness through rhythm, stomping and play, reached 12M+ views in 195 countries, 101K watch hours and 9,800 subscribers within 12 months from 300+ videos and Shorts, so big views can come with few subscribers on kids channels.

The Kiboomers (Canada, 4.04M subscribers) earns a steady 50 to 55M views a month while posting only one new video each Friday, and vidIQ models about 37K USD a month, far more per view than mass upload rhyme channels, because its catalogue is evergreen circle time music teachers replay.

All five of The Kiboomers' most viewed videos are movement games: Going on a Dragon Hunt (37.4M), Freeze Dance Song 2 (31.1M), Red Light Freeze Dance (30M), Going on a Dinosaur Hunt (23.4M) and Floor is Lava 2 Freeze Dance (18.2M), and sequels of a winning game (Freeze Dance 2, Floor is Lava 2) do as well as originals.

The Kiboomers' newest upload is a seasonal movement game, Shake Your Santa Hat (6 Nov 2026), so classroom channels release Christmas dance songs in the first week of November to catch teachers' December planning.

Kaboochi (2.17M subscribers, 2,225 videos) gets about 11.6M views a month, and its biggest hits are theme twists on the Finger Family song (Football Finger Family 29M, Planet Finger Family 17M), so a known song frame plus a new theme is its main growth trick, though sheer volume gives low views per video.

In Tubefilter's most subscribed list for the week of 8 Nov 2026 only three kids or family channels made the top 50: Pokemon Kids TV (Japan, about 400K new subscribers, down 20%), Cadel and Mia (about 300K) and VocaVoca Kids Songs (US, about 300K), so a nursery song channel like VocaVoca can still out gain most of YouTube.

CoComelon's owner Moonbug launched The Melon Patch on YouTube (season 2 from 23 Jul 2026), a live action show led by a music teacher host with acoustic nursery rhymes, original songs and real children singing along in new 15 minute episodes every other week, a move towards the warm human host style Ms Rachel proved.

Moonbug's content chief says the company is YouTube first, a brand must build a strong YouTube audience before toys, live tours and streaming deals, and content should fit each viewing moment from a short clip on a phone in the car to living room co viewing; its 2026 slate adds a Little Angel spin off with pop songs and pretend play for ages 3 to 5.

VocaVoca's last 28 days to 12 Nov 2026 brought about 1.42B views versus 2.91B in October, so even a fast rising song channel roughly halved its monthly reach once the Halloween spike passed; seasonal surges must be followed at once by the next season's songs.

VocaVoca's newest upload, a good manners song ('May I Please?', 11 Nov 2026), reached about 133K views in its first 13 hours, more evidence that manners, habits and safety songs are this channel's engine after Halloween.

Jasmin and James (Germany based duo, 43.1M subs, 79.9B views from about 26,700 videos) get their best recent Shorts from behind the scenes bloopers (120K to 188K views) and 'Can you do it?' challenges, ahead of plain trend tutorials; a Bro Bros bloopers Short (a brother slipping on a dance move) and a direct 'Can you do it?' challenge are cheap, proven formats.

Jasmin and James lean on movie character trend tutorials (Spider-Verse costume trends); we skip anything using protected characters and copy only the tutorial format (slow step, then full speed) with our own Bros.

Acamar Films (Bing) launched Again! Again!, a gentle paced public service style preschool channel on YouTube in June 2026 with presenter led themed blocks, live streamed segments and nine starter titles; Acamar already runs 67 channels in 33 languages with 1.3M viewing hours a day.

Lalafun's top recent breakout 'Catch the Black Sheep! Baa Baa Song' reached 33M views in about two months, 30 times its median, and its other hits follow the same title shape: an urgent mission for the baby ('Baby Helps the Itsy Bitsy Spider', 'Paramedic Cures the Boo Boos'), then a well known rhyme anchor, one or two emojis and the channel tag.

Lalafun has only 77 videos but 158M views, uploads about three long videos a week averaging nearly 18 minutes with no Shorts, and its estimated audience is the US 44%, UK 17%, Brazil 17%, Turkey 11% and Poland 11%.

Super Simple Songs' best recent upload is a remake of its own 'The Animals On The Farm' (38M views, 5.7 times median), and it now publishes 'High Contrast Kids Video' versions of songs (Fruit Is Yummy, 11M), so remaking our own proven hits and making high contrast baby editions are both proven moves.

Super Simple Songs still uploads only about once a week, recent uploads average about 30 minutes, long form gives 96% of its views, and its estimated audience is the US 53%, UK 18%, Canada 12%, Japan 12% and Vietnam 6%, showing English songs travel to ESL markets in Asia.

Kids Diana Show's recent breakouts are scale challenges ('10 vs 100 vs 1,000,000 House Decorating', 43M) and opposite pairs ('Ice Princess vs Fire Princess', 57M) plus story compilations, formats an animated channel can copy as '1 snowman vs 100 snowmen vs 1,000,000 snowmen' style songs.

Big kids channels keep about 85 to 90% evergreen content and only 10 to 15% trend based (Lalafun and Kids Diana 90/10, Super Simple Songs 85/15), a useful split for planning our 14 songs a week: roughly 12 evergreen and 2 trend songs.

Cocomelon's Instagram (about 790K followers, 1.1K posts) runs as a parenting humour and toddler life account aimed at adults, averaging about 214K Reel plays but only 0.26% likes per follower and about 10 posts in two weeks, far smaller than its YouTube reach.

Rhymington Square (Canada, 311K subscribers) has 291M views from only 74 videos, about 3.9M per video, built on original friendly monster songs about toddler life; few, strong, rewatchable songs can out earn a big volume of weaker ones.

Rhymington Square's recent breakouts are everyday toddler moments told as songs ('It's Way Too Hot Today' 17M, 'Let's Blow A Bubble' 16M, 'My Glasses' 10M) and numbered sequels of proven hits ('There's A Monster In My Tummy #2', 'Open Shut Them #2').

Seasonal holiday songs are Rhymington Square's largest topic cluster (15 of 74 videos) and about 24% of its content is trend based, with audience in the US 61%, Canada 21%, UK 12% and Australia 6%, so holiday songs suit North American audiences especially.

TinkaBop Baby Sensory, a young baby sensory music channel, had 11 videos and about 5K subscribers by Sep 2026 with a gentle bath time song as its best (18K views), showing how slowly a new routine song channel grows and how bath, wake up and bedtime routines lead in the baby niche.

OutlierKit flags dependence on YouTube Kids distribution and on one signature voice as key risks for small baby music channels, so Bro Bros should keep the Bros' voices consistent but build reach on main YouTube, Shorts and Instagram too.

Cocomelon's biggest 2026 breakouts stack two proven hooks in one title ('Yes Yes Finger Family Playground Song' 52M views, 14 times its median; 'The Rainbow Popsicle Cafe + Super Muffin Man' 21M) or revive a novelty classic ('Bananaphone' 40M).

Cocomelon still uploads about three videos a week averaging about 5.5 minutes with almost no Shorts, keeps about 95% evergreen content, and roughly 10% of recent uploads are Hello Kitty and Sanrio collaborations, showing big brands now team up with other kids IP for fresh reach.
Cocomelon's estimated audience is the US 50%, India 17%, UK 17%, Canada 11% and Australia 6%, so India is now as big as the UK for English nursery songs.

Ms Rachel uploads only about 1.4 videos a month but each runs about 45 minutes, and her top titles lead with a parent search promise ('Baby Learning with Ms Rachel', 'Learn to Talk', 'First Words', '2 Year Old Milestones') before 'Nursery Rhymes & Kids Songs', proof that parents search by developmental goal.

An exploratory academic study of English and Portuguese AI made kids videos (2022 to 2024) found music and stories are the main content types, most such videos get low view counts with a few viral exceptions, and many sit on a spectrum of partial AI use; a Bro Bros edge is visible human craft (story, choreography, edits) on top of AI tools.
leaves.src: AoIR Selected Papers (Mintz and Bozzi), Jan 2026

leaves.t: Super Simple Songs turned 20 in 2026 with over 70M subscribers and 90B views; it began in 2006 as teachers abroad posting songs to help children learn English, so English learning classrooms worldwide are a lasting audience Bro Bros can serve with clear, slow, repeatable English lyrics.

Super Simple's maker Skyship moved to a self funded Toronto studio in 2015 with 40+ in house animators, musicians, puppeteers and educators, and works with researchers (an Oxford University Press project in Spain) on how music shapes early learning, using that teaching credibility to win parents and teachers.

Moonbug says Little Angel has over 150M YouTube subscribers and about 1.4B monthly views across 25 languages, and it programmes its linear channels in 100+ countries around daily routines from morning to bedtime (meals, tooth brushing, bedtime), the same routine slots Bro Bros playlists should be named for.

Moonbug's 2026 plan is YouTube first but non exclusive ('be on every platform where kids and families are'), extending hit IP into Spotify music, toys and live tours, and it is pushing hardest into Southern Europe (Spain and France), a sign those markets reward kids brands now.

Mother Goose Club licensed its YouTube library to the SKIDOS ad free learning app for ages 2 and up (Aug 2026), showing a later revenue path for a big kids song catalogue: subscription learning apps that pay for familiar, education framed content.

Moonbug's Blippi spinoff Meekah opened on its own YouTube channel on 7 Nov 2026, warmed up by a single music video ('Happy Place') on 2 Nov, with roughly 15 minute episodes for ages 3 to 6 every other Saturday.

Meekah episodes alternate short bursts of dance and physical play with short pauses, a move then rest rhythm built on UCLA backed learning principles that Bro Bros can copy inside long compilations (dance, calm breath, dance).

Moonbug launched Big Feelings Music in Sept 2026, offering label services, publishing administration and YouTube distribution to outside children's music creators, a possible future partner route for an independent kids song brand.

Pinkfong is releasing the soundtrack of its 5 Dec Baby Shark Christmas sing along film in two waves (10 Nov and 27 Nov), 15 tracks with seven new songs, and uses an on screen MC character to lead audience participation, a staged drop pattern we can copy for a December song pack.

ChuChu TV grew by refreshing old nursery rhymes with new stories instead of making lullabies, and even early on earned 40 to 50% of revenue abroad (mostly UK, US and Canada) while Vietnam gave many views but little revenue.

Kids Diana's network is 32 channels in 17 languages with about 429M subscribers and 261B views; its 27 smaller language channels together have about 240M subscribers, more than the 138M main channel, showing that separate dubbed channels can outgrow the original.

Kids Diana's largest language channels are Spanish (41.1M), Arabic (30.9M), English (30M) and Hindi (29.4M), and about 12 of its channels run 24/7 live streams, while the main channel has added multi language audio tracks.

In Tubefilter's week of 8 Nov 2026, Spanish preschool channel El Tren Nam Nam dropped 52% (from No. 7 to No. 39) while Keizo and Friends climbed from No. 29 to No. 20 and two Sierra and Rhia channels sat in the top 8, showing how fast kids channel weekly views swing.

A Spanish kids channel admitted to the YouTube Kids app about a month after an official partner submitted it saw views grow 396%, with the app supplying 67.4% of its traffic, so getting Bro Bros reviewed for the Kids app is one of the biggest single growth levers once the catalogue is clean.

AIR's order of fixes for a stalled kids channel is trust signals first (clean thumbnails, remove weak old videos, resolve yellow icons), then dubbed audio tracks, then 24/7 streams, because languages and streams only work once YouTube trusts the channel.

BabyBus (44.2M subscribers, about 186M views in the last 28 days) has slowed sharply in 2026: about 100K new subscribers a month versus 300K to 700K in 2024, and monthly views fell from about 328M in April to 218M in October 2026.

BabyBus's most watched videos are still older evergreen songs (Rainbow Juice colours song from 2022 at 147M views), while its 2025 and 2026 'Sharing is Caring' good habit songs are the clear outliers at 10 to 16 times the channel's normal views, so manners and feelings songs keep pulling new viewers.

CoComelon's Portuguese channel posted 48 uploads between 31 Aug and 9 Nov 2026 (29 long videos, median 5:22, and 19 Shorts, median 22 seconds), roughly five uploads a week split about 3 long to 2 Shorts.

CoComelon's dubbed channels tag brand new songs with a star and the word NEW at the start of the title and still publish 30 minute holiday compilations, and their best recent long uploads are simple action or routine songs (a rain go away song at 4.7M, a car wash song at 2.4M).

Brazil's kid pop acts show how fast a school age music brand can grow: duo Kysha e Mine reached about 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in roughly a year with a school themed series, and MC Divertida has about 18.3M subscribers; their label has psychologists review lyrics and scripts, which it says wins parent and school trust.

Disney Jr. tests stories with children through an internal panel and feeds results to writers (its programming head calls young viewers 'our bosses'), and grew SuperKitties over three years with 60 minute specials, shorts and long episodes side by side, so one Bro Bros song should also ship as a Short, a long video and a compilation slot.

Pinkfong launched 'Baby Shark Boy' in Aug 2026 with the single 'WAVE', which opens on the familiar Baby Shark melody and grows into upbeat electropop with trap beats and a featured K-pop rapper, plus a point choreography that nods to the original dance but stays easy to follow, a way to keep kids who have outgrown nursery songs.

Pinkfong's new Baby Shark musical (2 Dec 2026 to 28 Mar 2027, Seoul) has no seats: children roam seven themed zones, join missions, hold colour changing microphones and their voices become part of the music, and the story is about recovering a lost rhythm and melody, showing that 'help us fix the song' participation is the brand's next step.

Russian language family creator Sasha Show grew from about 1.2 to 2.2M new subscribers a month in mid 2026 to 9.47M in October (18.3M total, 633M views in the last 28 days) with only about 46 uploads a year of toy, candy and bath challenge videos and remixes, yet vidIQ models only about 17K USD of earnings, showing how little very large Shorts led kids audiences can pay.

Toys and Colors' franchise reported 136M subscribers and 149B lifetime views, with its top three YouTube channels reaching 348M unique viewers and 11.6B minutes of watch time in 90 days, and its holiday special came with an original single released on Spotify, Amazon Music and Apple Music, so a kids channel's holiday song should also live on music apps.

Sasha Show's titles lean on famous toy and candy brands and extreme 'who will win' challenges, a growth route Bro Bros should not copy (brand names invite claims and do not suit made for kids quality rules), but its question style titles ('Who will...?') match the mystery question hooks already in our playbook.

Bebefinn's main English channel (37.3M subscribers, 25.1B views, 1,086 videos since Mar 2022) still adds about 370M views a month, but its subscriber gains fell to 100K to 300K a month in 2026 from 500K to 1.3M a month in 2024 and 2025, the same plateau BabyBus and Little Angel show, so the biggest 3D song brands are no longer growing fast and newer channels have room.

Bebefinn's newest upload, 'We Are Car Mechanics! Let's Fix the Car!' (13 Nov 2026), drew about 133K views in 13 hours with a title built as emoji, pretend play job and action call, and its all time top video is a 2022 good morning wake up routine song (775M views), so pretend play jobs and daily routine songs remain the brand's core.

vidIQ models Bebefinn's main channel at only about 97K USD a month of ad revenue from roughly 370M monthly views (about 0.26 USD per 1,000 views), confirming that made for kids song views earn little per view and that brands like Pinkfong earn mainly from streaming deals, toys and live shows.

Indonesian kids family channel Keizo and Friends (started Dec 2022) reached about 9.9M subscribers and 39.2B views from 1,998 uploads by Oct 2026, adding about 1.65B views and 390K subscribers in 28 days, with a new upload passing 1.5M views in 14 hours; vidIQ models only about 9K USD a month, so its scale comes from Shorts views in a low pay market.

AIR's study of 282 kids channels found the largest (10M to 50M monthly views) earned the most total revenue at 16+ videos a month, but each video then earned only about 165 USD against about 2,161 USD per video for channels posting one or two a month, so our 14 songs a week buy reach, while a few polished flagship songs per month carry most of the money.

Keizo and Friends' all time top video is from 7 Dec 2025 (about 626M views), a December upload that kept growing for a year, another sign that early December family videos get a long tail and our holiday songs should be live by the first week of December.

Skyship's live action 'Super Simple Play with Caitie!' (Canada, 5.25M subscribers) steadied at about 47 to 58M views a month through 2026 after a 2025 peak (332M in Apr 2025); its all time hits are 'Here Comes the Fire Truck' (109M), the colour hunt 'I See Something Blue' (78M), a Halloween knock knock song (63M) and the freeze game 'Can You Dance and Stop?' (50M), and vidIQ models about 46K USD a month.

US rhyme channel Super Supremes (4M subscribers, 960 videos) has been flat since late 2025 at about 3 to 7M views a month and its newest Short (9 Nov 2026, a fire truck wheels song) drew only about 1.8K views in five days, showing that a big but stale subscriber base no longer guarantees views for generic rhyme remakes.

Across both channels the top songs are fire trucks, Halloween and colour or freeze games, and Caitie's newest upload (12 Nov) is already a Christmas party song, so Super Simple starts holiday uploads in mid November.

Five of the ten most viewed YouTube videos of all time are children's songs (led by Baby Shark Dance and CoComelon's Wheels on the Bus), together estimated at about 84M USD in ad revenue, proof that one evergreen kids song can earn for years.

Lalafun's 'Learning Time!' side channel (605K subscribers, only 91 videos) was flat until May 2026, then jumped to about 34 to 61M views a month from July to October; its hits put a verb and a baby helper into a classic rhyme title ('Catch the Black Sheep!' 76M, 'Baby Helps the Itsy Bitsy Spider!' 31M, 'Animals Go to a Picnic! Wheels on the Bus' 20M).

Funny Lala, Lalafun's kindergarten channel (1.77M subscribers, 326 videos since Jun 2023), still gains about 80K subscribers and 72M views a month, and all of its top five videos are remixes of rhymes into little stories (a rainy farm 'where is the sun?' remix leads at 31.5M).

Lalafun's Canada feed has 2,408 videos and 1.64M subscribers, yet its 31 Oct 2026 toothbrush song drew only 495 views in 41 hours while the brand's young Learning Time channel got about 25K views in under two days on its newest upload, so the algorithm rewards fresh focused channels over huge back catalogues.

Both healthy Lalafun channels title new songs as an action plus a familiar character or animal ('Catch the Little Frogs with Baby Lala!', 'Five Little Ducklings and Mommy Duck'), mixing a known rhyme cue with a small adventure, which is a title pattern we can copy with our own originals ('Catch the Snowflakes with Little Bro!').

Jason Vlogs, two brothers' kids channel that grew from 23M to 46M+ subscribers with a peak of about 1B views in one month, keeps a baseline of one main video a week with extras as bonuses, plans and batches weeks ahead, and runs on a core team of five.

Jason Vlogs brainstorms about 30 ideas a week and produces only 3, filtering by current platform trends, what kids already react to and whether the idea stays fun and teaches something, a stricter filter than making every idea that comes up.

ChuChu TV's newest English uploads (Oct to Nov 2026) are 24 to 34 minute story and learning compilations: 'Celebrate and Shine', a combined Diwali and Christmas story video, reached about 197K views in 16 days, a surprise egg colour song about 140K in 9 days and a learning story set about 15K in 2 days, so even a 98M subscriber channel's new uploads start small and the library carries it.

ChuChu TV tested a 2 minute read along toddler story with copy the duck play actions ('Hello, Ducklings!'), which drew about 94K views in 25 days, close to its long compilations, showing short copy me action stories are a cheap format worth testing beside songs.

Little Angel Playtime (3.24M subscribers) fell from about 10.5M monthly views in Aug 2026 to 8.6M, 7.5M and then 4.9M in October, and its newest song ('Eye Tests Are Not Scary!', 14 Nov) had under 1K views after 11 hours, showing that even a famous brand's spin off channel fades when it keeps posting small routine topics without fresh hooks.

Little Angel and Friends (7.3M subscribers, about 26M views in Oct 2026) earns mostly from 2021 to 2022 songs: Baa Baa Black Sheep 601M, a bedtime 'Monsters Under the Bed' song 210M and a lollipops, balloons and sunglasses colours song 205M; its new Baby John Wheels on the Bus vehicle song had about 3.7K views in 10 hours.

Super Simple Songs' uploads from late August to mid October 2026 were mostly 'Top 20' themed mixes (about 0.8 to 1.2M views each) and two 'Super Simple Live!' Halloween streams, while a single party song, 'Everybody Celebrate' (27 Aug), reached 6M, the clear outlier; a celebration song for any party day can outperform themed compilations.

Pinkfong launched Kikipuppup (with Japan's TBS) on YouTube first, in English, Japanese and Korean, as about 3 minute slapstick episodes with a cat, a dog and a grumpy rival, and is rolling out a wordless comedy (SEALOOK) in Russia, so the biggest song brand is adding short, dialogue light comedy that travels without dubbing.

Pinkfong keeps refreshing Baby Shark through partner remixes: a 'Do The Shark' remix in Doggyland's style, a Baby Shark and Peppa Pig mash up for the song's 10th anniversary (26 Dec 2025), and a Bebefinn medley with the London Symphony Orchestra; a hit song can be re released many times in new styles.

The Blocks Universe (Numberblocks, Alphablocks) launched its first Christmas single, 'Making Christmas Magical' with K-pop group FIFTY FIFTY, as two videos of the same song a week apart (a live action dance video on 28 Nov, the animated video on 5 Dec) plus a printables hub, a model for getting two premieres out of one holiday song.

Blippi's strongest Shorts of early November 2026 are timed challenges and playground games: 'Can Blippi build a rocket in 45 seconds?' (about 130K views, 2x its usual) and 'Red Light Green Light with kids' (about 198K), so a 'Can the Bro Bros build a snowman in 30 seconds?' countdown Short fits what kids are clicking now.

Blippi's titles in November follow one pattern: a direct question with the character's name plus a challenge or a 'what if' ('What would Blippi look like as an animal?', 'Can a fire truck be as fast as a race car?'), with one or two emojis; the same pattern works for us as 'Can Vihaan ...?' or 'What if the Bro Bros ...?' Shorts titles.
