On kids channels the voice is part of the product, and an AI voice that sounds too adult, flat or emotionally off can hurt retention and even draw misleading content flags, so Bro Bros dubs should be sung by real or carefully cast child like voices, not YouTube's default auto dub.

Good human dubs can match or beat the original: a kids channel with an Indonesian original (165M views) held 2:11 on its pro Spanish track against 2:00 on the original, and Turkish, Italian and German tracks stayed close.

On one kids channel with the same videos dubbed three ways, Arabic brought the most views (3.4M) but German, with only 134K views, had the highest share of returning viewers (about 52%) and the longest watch time, so small markets can be the most loyal.

AIR judges a new dubbed language by the share of its views that come from casual plus regular (returning) viewers: under 20% after four months is a problem, 20 to 40% is building, over 40% is working and over 60% is strong, and the first 90 days are too early to judge.

CIMM's July 2026 report says US young children's video time is now about 35% streaming, 32% YouTube and 16% short form (TikTok, Shorts), with linear TV down to about 6% from 80 to 90% in 2005, and children make up nearly a quarter of all YouTube viewing.

US children aged 0 to 8 now average about 2 hours 27 minutes of screen time a day (up from 1 hour 44 in 2005), with mobile the main device, while YouTube Analytics only shows demographics for viewers 13 and over, so our own analytics can never show the true age of our audience.

Kenya's Akili TV added read along captions to existing cartoons in a 'Read Along Hour' (Swahili and French pilots) and child viewing rose about 15% while adult co viewing rose about 39%, so big on screen karaoke style lyrics in Bro Bros songs can draw parents in and help reading.

At least 14 kids and family channels sit in France's top 100 YouTube channels by subscribers (11 Nov 2026), led by Masha et Michka (12.2M), Kidi Fun (11.9M), Titounis comptines (7.7M), Kidibli (7.5M) and Little Angel's French channel (5.7M), so French is a strong second language market for nursery songs.

International song brands run separate French channels that rank high in France (Little Angel French 5.7M, HeyKids French 4.9M and its English channel also in France's top 100 at 4.8M), showing French parents subscribe to both local language and English kids song channels.

Kaboochi's French channel (197K subscribers, 618 videos) earned only about 135K views in the 28 days to 29 Oct 2026 after its uploads stopped in September, with Shorts as its best videos, so a dubbed language channel fades fast without steady uploads; audio tracks on the main channel are safer for a small team.

Spotify Wrapped 2025 coverage from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa says children now shape whole household listening there, with Cocomelon nursery rhymes, Baby Shark and gentle singalongs like You Are My Sunshine topping family recaps, used for mornings, car rides and bedtime and spread through siblings and cousins sharing one phone.

In an AIR test where one kids channel ran the same videos, thumbnails and schedule in Arabic, French and German (16 Feb to 24 Mar 2026), Arabic drew by far the most views (3.4M in five weeks against 745K French and 134K German), confirming Arabic as a high volume first dub for kids songs.

In the same test German viewers were the most loyal (about 52% returning, 10.6% regular, new viewers averaging 4:30 against 2:49 for Arabic), so smaller rich markets can repay a dub through watch time and higher ad rates even with fewer views.

AIR suggests judging each dubbed audio track by returning viewers, not views: in YouTube Analytics' 'Audience by watch behaviour' filtered by audio track, casual plus regular viewers above 40% means the language is working, 20 to 40% is building and below 20% after four months needs fixing; this share should climb about 3 to 5 points a month in the first year.

On one entertainment channel the Spanish dubbed track's viewers watched about two minutes longer per view than the English original (8:55 against 6:59), which AIR puts down to less competition in Spanish.

Audiences in Russia, Germany, Italy, Spain, Mexico, Brazil and France prefer dubbing, while adults in China, South Korea, India and Japan prefer subtitles; young children everywhere need dubbing because they cannot read subtitles fast enough, so for kids songs only re sung audio tracks count as localisation.

Only about 13% of creators in AIR's 3,000 channel network have paid for professional dubbing and 36% have tried AI dubbing, yet dubbed tracks averaged about 45% more views and YouTube says creators with dubbed tracks get over 25% of watch time from non primary languages, so early dubbing is still a gap Bro Bros can use.

One small counter example: a creator's dedicated Spanish channel got 3,897 views in 90 days against just 32 for the same video's Spanish track on his main English channel, so a separate language channel may beat audio tracks when the main channel has little audience in that language.

In Latin America children aged 3 to 5 use only YouTube for screen content, subscription apps appear around age 6 and games around 9 to 12, so a Spanish and Portuguese dub of our preschool songs reaches the youngest kids on the one screen they all share.

Kidscorp finds YouTube is the only screen with similar reach across high, middle and low income homes in Latin America, reaching about 68% of under 18s in Mexico and Chile versus under 30% for TV, and above 70% digital adoption in Brazil and Argentina.

Across 16 MENA markets kids animation is 40.6% of supply but only 30.2% of demand, while US and Japanese titles drive over 85% of animation demand, so a new kids channel there competes in a crowded field and must stand out with quality and Arabic audio.

Children aged 0 to 14 are about a quarter of MENA's population, and parents stay closely involved in judging whether content fits family values, so modest outfits, kind behaviour and no romance matter for Arabic speaking families.

Pan Arab kids hits mix dialects (the Mansour reboot blends Emirati, Saudi, Iraqi, Egyptian and other voices) and the original Mansour drew most of its 2.5B views from outside the UAE, notably Iraq and Egypt, so an Arabic dub should use simple, widely understood Arabic rather than one local dialect.

Sanrio launched 'Sanrio Kids - Cartoons & Kids Songs' on YouTube on 15 Sep 2026 as a global preschool channel whose 3D videos carry Japanese and English audio switchable within the same video, the same multi audio track route open to Bro Bros.

Sanrio Kids splits its channel into three series (sing along music, movement and play including calming down, and everyday story episodes), each about two minutes, a clean playlist structure for a song brand entering Japan and Asia.

In a Philippine survey of 1,000 parents (29 Oct to 2 Nov 2026), 34% named child specific apps such as YouTube Kids as a safety measure and 97% wanted evidence based rules for children's social media, so Filipino families value clearly kid safe channels.

The same survey found 60% of Filipino parents say their children use social apps for rest and relaxation and 70% for learning, which favours calm songs and learning songs in Filipino focused playlists.

Vietnam's first music video to pass 1B YouTube views (June 2024) is the kids song 'Mot con vit' about a mother duck and five yellow ducklings, sung by a three year old, from a channel with only about 40 short songs under five minutes; other kids songs hold several of Vietnam's next biggest totals (crocodile song 665M), so a simple animal family song can top a whole country's music charts.

Vietnamese parents use the duck song as a mealtime helper to get children to eat, the same 'song for a daily routine' role our habit songs aim for, so mealtime songs are a strong fit for Vietnam and other Southeast Asian homes.

POPS Kids, Vietnam's largest kids channel, has about 20.3M subscribers and 15B views from 4,687 videos (Oct 2026), mixing its own shows with licensed Doraemon and Pokemon cartoons, and drew about 3.5M views on a single day; Social Blade puts its income anywhere from about 94K to 7.2M USD a year, showing how wide and unreliable such estimates are.

Nigerian YouTube watch time grew over 50% in a year and views for one network's Nigerian creators rose from 70M to over 400M, yet Nigerian ads pay only about 0.5 to 2.5 USD per 1,000 views against up to 15 USD in the US, so for Bro Bros, Nigeria and other English speaking African homes are reach and word of mouth markets, not revenue markets.

Germany's 'Kinderlieder zum Mitsingen und Bewegen' channel has 3.47M subscribers, about 33 to 43M views a month from 1,453 videos and vidIQ models about 14K USD a month; it wraps new titles in 'NEU * ... * NEU', its newest song (13 Nov 2026) teaches tying a bow, and its top videos are remixes of singing games such as 'who stole the cookie from the jar' (24.4M) and a dog's lost bone song (22.9M).

Japan's most viewed kids songs on YouTube are franchise themes (a monster catching game theme at 105M), Japanese language versions of Disney songs and songs from the public TV show 'Okaasan to Issho' (a clock song, a bean hero song), so Japanese children mostly watch Japanese language content and an English Bro Bros song has little pull there until it is re sung in Japanese.

German and Japanese hits both lean on practical everyday skills and objects (tying a bow, telling the time), which suggests life skill songs translate across cultures better than culture specific holidays.

Pakistan's top YouTube channels in Nov 2026 are led by family and Shorts creators: 16 family tagged channels sit in the top 90, including Ak Ultra (19M subscribers, 22.3B views), Anaya Eshaal Family (16.9M) and Minsa Saim Omer (13.4M, 20.9B views), so Pakistani children mostly watch family creators, and an animated English song channel has to win them through Shorts.

Urdu story channel Geo Kahani has about 7M subscribers and 4.5B views in Pakistan's top 60, which suggests narrated animated stories in Urdu are a large format there, similar to the Hindi story videos we already make.

Pakistani learning channel TinyTaleem still has 145K subscribers but drew only about 2,500 views in October 2026 from 453 videos (top videos are English ABC and animal name lessons and an Urdu alphabet poem), a reminder that a subscriber count means little once a channel stops posting fresh, recommendable videos.

In Bangladesh's top 100 YouTube channels (vidIQ, 12 Nov 2026) there is no nursery rhyme or kids music channel; children's attention goes to craft and drawing giants (Tonni art and craft 19.5M subscribers, Farjana Drawing Academy 15.6M, Mukta Art and Craft 8.2M) and Maasranga Kids (5.3M, 4.9B views), so a Bengali dub of our songs would face little direct competition.

Draw along videos are among the biggest family formats in Bangladesh (three drawing or craft channels in the top 60), which supports a 'draw Little Bro step by step' Short with our song playing as a cheap extra format for South Asian viewers.

Poland's most subscribed YouTube channels (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026) include dubbed foreign kids brands (WB Kids 7.1M, Cartoonito Polska 3.6M, Masha 2.8M, Peppa Pig and Disney Junior 1.8M each) beside local rhyme channel Singing Toddlers (2.6M) and family creator Hejka tu Lenka (1.8M), so Polish families accept dubbed animation readily.

HeyKids' Polish song channel (856K subscribers, 630M views) gets a steady 3.5 to 5M views a month in 2026 with almost no subscriber growth; its top songs are about a cheeky little boy character (19.3M), construction machines (6.9M) and a red car (5.7M), the same vehicle and mischief themes that win elsewhere.

Jason Vlogs runs 10 localised channels and says they did not cannibalise the main channel but brought in new viewers, another data point that separate language channels add audience rather than split it.

Thailand's top kids and family YouTube channels (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026) are mostly family vlogs and comedy: Vlad and Niki Thai 14.2M subscribers, J Jai Pan 13.5M, a slime toy channel 11.9M and YimYam TV 10.5M, while animal and learning song channels 'kids song' (7.7M) and KidsMeSong (7.4M) hold the music slots, so a Thai market favours playful sibling characters plus animal songs.

Moonbug Kids Arabic (dubbed Morphle and Blippi) has 909K subscribers and 369M lifetime views but only about 2M views a month in Oct 2026 and about 3.6K views on a new upload after three days, so a dubbed foreign brand channel grows slowly in Arabic; local feeling songs and titles matter more than the brand.

Moonbug Kids Arabic's all time hits are emotional story moments ('Morphing Family' 41M, 'Morphle is Alone and Cries' 25M) rather than songs, which hints Arabic speaking families respond to family and feelings stories; an Arabic Bro Bros pilot could start with a brothers and family feelings song.

Egypt's most subscribed YouTube channel (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026) is Kids Diana's Arabic channel 'Diana and Roma ARA' (30.9M), followed by family channels Osratouna TV (21.8M) and Marah TV (14.2M) and about ten Egyptian family comedy channels with 7 to 12M each, so Arabic family audiences favour dubbed sibling characters and family sketches over plain rhymes.

In Ukraine the second most watched kids YouTube channel is a local Ukrainian language song channel by Lviv authors (about 614M views), about half of the top 20 kids channels are in Ukrainian and the English 3D song brand Sandy the Sticker ranks No. 9 (74M), so a Ukrainian dub of our songs would meet strong demand for local language kids music.

English language animated kids channels still reach the top 10 in non English markets like Ukraine (two of the top 10: an Ali Baba channel and Sandy the Sticker) because music and movement carry without words, supporting our plan to grow first in English and add dubs where local demand is proven.

Brazil's ICT Kids Online 2025 survey (2,370 children aged 9 to 17, published May 2026) found 92% are internet users (about 24M children) and 60% of them go online through a television every day, so in Brazil the living room TV is a daily screen for kids, which rewards long form compilations with a Portuguese audio track.

In the same Brazilian survey phone ownership among 9 to 10 year olds fell to 55% (from 67% in 2024) and social media use in that age group dropped from 48% in 2021 to 33% in 2025, a sign that younger Brazilian children are moving toward shared family screens and supervised viewing rather than their own phones.

28% of Brazilian 9 to 17 year olds first went online by age 6, and 80% watch influencer videos, series or films online (46% watch influencer content several times a day), so a Brazilian family meets kids' video in the preschool years, the exact age band of Bro Bros songs.

BabyBus's Japanese channel (5.86M subscribers) still draws about 104M views every 28 days, but its monthly subscriber gains fell from about 150K in Dec 2025 to 20K in Oct 2026, so in a mature market views now come from catalogue and recommendations, not fresh subscriptions.

BabyBus's Vietnamese channel (9.75M subscribers, rank 33 in Vietnam) gets about 71M to 116M views a month in 2026 and a single new Short reached about 528K views in 2.5 days, so Vietnam (63M YouTube users) is a large kids market where a re sung Vietnamese track or Shorts could earn real volume.

Japan's kids songs on YouTube are led by anime and character themes (Pokémon, Doraemon, Anpanman) and songs from NHK's daily preschool show 'Okaasan to Issho' (a clock song, a noodle song), plus family pop such as Gen Hoshino's 'Family Song', so Japanese parents favour songs tied to a familiar show; a Japanese Bro Bros track works best on everyday routine topics like time, food and bath.

Nigeria has over 30M adult YouTube viewers, watch time grew over 50% in a year and views from Nigeria rose about 80% (Yoola data), with local CPMs of about 0.50 to 2.50 USD against up to 15 USD in the US; as an English speaking country it is a growing audience our English songs reach with no dubbing.

Both BabyBus local channels post Shorts and song live streams in local language (for example a Japanese ice cream song live stream on 13 Nov 2026), showing that the big brands run the same three formats (long songs, Shorts, live loops) in every language, not only in English.

About 80% of the content children consume in the Arab world is in languages other than Arabic, Abu Dhabi's culture chief said in September 2026, calling for a 50 50 split; with around 430M Arabic speakers this is a large, under served audience for a well voiced Arabic track.

Arabic lullaby videos are still scarce online: Spacetoon Mum and Moonbug launched just four original Arabic lullabies in June 2026 to fill the gap, so a calm Bro Bros bedtime song with a human voiced Arabic audio track could rank with little competition.

AIR's dubbing case data gives typical CPMs of about 0.84 USD for Indonesian, 1.52 Serbian, 1.77 Ukrainian, 2.56 Bulgarian, 3.10 Romanian, 3.69 Greek, 4.02 Hungarian, 5.23 Czech, 5.31 Polish and 9.79 German, so after the big reach languages, Polish, Czech and German tracks earn several times more per view.

Small language dubs can dominate local charts: an Indonesian kids animation channel (HZH, 12.5M subscribers, about 6.8B views) and the German dub of Vania Mania (1.21M subscribers, #7 in German kids entertainment) both grew from dubbed tracks, which AIR says sometimes beat the original in watch time.

In YouTube's weekly music charts for 19 to 25 Dec 2025, holiday songs filled the top 10 in the US, UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Australia, Portugal, Spain, France and Japan, but India, Brazil and South Africa had few or none, so for those big kids audiences our December slots should also carry winter, party and New Year songs, not only Christmas.

In Japan a Japanese language Christmas song by a local band sat at No. 3 on YouTube's chart in Christmas week 2025, beside the Western classics, so a Japanese audio track on our main Christmas song is worth testing for that market.

Infobells Hindi (about 72.8M subscribers) has stalled: +0.2M subscribers from May to August 2026 and no change from late September to mid October, with total views rising about 2.2B in four and a half months (roughly 450M a month), so India's oldest rhyme giants are mature and new Hindi entrants face an open, not closed, market.

Kids Channel India (Hindi rhymes, 44.1M subscribers) drew between about 311M and 497M views a month in 2026 (432M in October, its best since January) and +200K to +400K subscribers a month; its newest upload is an elephant rhyme Short ('Ek Mota Hathi', about 284K views in under two days), showing animal rhymes still lead in Hindi.

El Reino Infantil's Spanish network passed 5.6B YouTube views from January to April 2026 across channels with 229M subscribers, and backs YouTube with more than 90 licensing deals in 15 countries, 2.2M merchandise units and live tours in the Americas and Spain; Spanish kids audiences reward one loved cast built over many years.

Brazil's biggest kids music stars are home grown 'pop infantil' acts: MC Divertida (about 18.3M subscribers, 8.6B plays) and the duo Kysha e Mine (about 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in roughly a year, its school life series 'Lance de Escola' over 350M views), built on YouTube plus TikTok plus sold out live shows and family friendly values.

Junior Squad Português, a separate Brazilian dub of an animated nursery channel (813K subscribers), is fading: monthly views fell from about 2.7M in March 2026 to 0.8M in October, subscribers are flat and its newest Short got about 300 views in three days, more proof that a stand alone dubbed channel without new local originals withers while multi audio tracks on the main channel keep the main channel's signals.

Junior Squad Português's all time top videos are a five little monkeys rhyme (46M), a boo boo song (14M) and a peekaboo song (14M), all from 2021 to 2022, showing that in Portuguese the same evergreen topics (counting rhymes, small hurts, peekaboo) lead as in English.

Kids Tv Bangla (3.69M subscribers) gets about 55M views every 28 days but vidIQ models only about 2,500 USD a month in ads, roughly 0.05 USD per 1,000 views, so Bengali language views bring reach but almost no income compared with English views from rich countries.

That channel's strongest recent upload is an August 2026 remake of an old Bengali folk rhyme (9.3M views, about 68 times its usual), so in South Asian markets refreshed classic local rhymes still beat new songs; for us that argues for original songs in English first and local dubs later, not local rhyme remakes.

HypeAuditor's top 100 Pakistani YouTube channels by subscribers (Nov 2026) are led by TV networks and dramas (Geo, ARY, HUM) and contain no kids or nursery rhyme channel, which suggests Pakistani children mostly watch global English or Hindi and Urdu kids channels from abroad.

Bengali rhyme channels grow steadily rather than in spikes (Kids Tv Bangla has added about 35M to 90M views a month since late 2024 and about 40K to 50K subscribers a month), the slow and steady pattern of a library of evergreen rhymes and compilations.

vidIQ models LooLoo's Spanish channel at only about 20K USD from about 154M monthly views (roughly 0.13 USD per 1,000), so Spanish language kids views pay several times less than English ones, though more than Bengali ones.

The Vietnamese BabyBus channel's most viewed long videos are all December 2021 to 2022 uploads (Kiki and friends 26M, a sushi song 24M, a mystery gift box 23M), showing that its library peaked years ago and new long videos rarely overtake old winners, while new Shorts still reach about 500K views in two days.

vidIQ models BabyBus's Vietnamese channel at only about 3,500 USD a month from about 92M monthly views (roughly 0.04 USD per 1,000), among the lowest earning kids audiences we have measured, so Vietnamese dubs are for reach, not income.

A December 2025 look at Spotify Wrapped in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa found kids' picks (CoComelon, Pinkfong, Super Simple Songs, Wheels on the Bus, Baby Shark) became the whole household's soundtrack, used for morning prep, car rides, bath and bedtime, alongside local language lullabies, so routine songs travel well in African homes.

Kids Tv Bangla (3.69M subscribers, about 2.1B views) gets about 52M to 59M views a month in 2026, yet vidIQ models only about 2,500 USD of ad income from that, roughly 0.05 USD per 1,000 views, so a Bengali dub would add reach and fans but very little money.

Kids Tv Bangla's three most viewed videos are remix versions of traditional Bengali rhymes (15M to 18M each), and an August 2026 traditional rhyme upload reached 9.3M views in under three months, 68 times its usual video, so in South Asian markets a remixed folk rhyme beats new material.

Bangladesh has about 45 million children and too little local children's content, so many kids watch Indian Hindi cartoons on YouTube and some speak Hindi better than Bengali, which makes a Hindi dub reach Bangladeshi children too (article undated, early to mid 2020s).

HypeAuditor's November 2026 Thailand ranking puts localised editions of global family brands in its top ten family channels (Vlad and Niki THA 14.2M subscribers, Brianna's Secret Club TH 8.2M) next to local Thai family channels of 6M to 13.5M, so a separately localised Thai channel of a global brand can reach the top there.

Thai preschool song channels stay small next to Thai family vlogs: Little Treehouse Thailand, a kindergarten songs channel, has about 223K subscribers and 83M views, growing about 4% a month, while the biggest Thai kids song channels (kids song 7.7M, KidsMeSong 7.4M) are a fraction of the top family channels.

LooLoo's Polish channel (about 200K subscribers, 103M views, 622 videos) slid from about 1.8M monthly views in July 2026 to about 0.8M in October and vidIQ models only about 200 USD a month, so Polish is a small, low paying dub market to add late, not early.

LooLoo Polish's two biggest videos are 30 and 40 minute compilations led by a marching ants song (about 5.3M and 4.7M views), so the marching ants theme that gave our best Reel this week (Ant Parade) also travels to Eastern Europe and suits a long compilation opener.

CoComelon Italiano has only about 1.2M subscribers and 1.3B views from 939 uploads; its October 2026 Halloween Shorts drew about 3K to 10K views each while a long seasonal vegetables episode reached about 161K within a week, so in Italy even the biggest brand's Shorts are weak and long episodes carry the channel.

Thailand's YouTube top 100 (Nov 2026) includes Thai editions of global kids brands (Vlad and Niki Thai 14.2M subscribers, Brianna's Secret Club TH 8.2M) and three Thai language kids song channels with about 7.1M to 7.7M subscribers and 4B to 4.6B views each, so a Thai dubbed Bro Bros channel would enter a large, song hungry market despite the small language.

Nine of Italy's top 100 YouTube channels (vidIQ, 12 Nov 2026) are for kids, mostly Italian editions of global brands (Masha e Orso 7.3M subscribers at 12th, WB Kids Italiano 5.4M, Disney Junior Italia 3.8M, Nickelodeon Italia 2.6M) plus local song brands HeyKids (3.4M, 3.4B views), Dolci Melodie (3.0M) and Coccole Sonore (2.6M), so Italian families readily watch dubbed foreign cartoons and an Italian song channel has room.

Turkey's top animation channel list (Nov 2026) has no large kids song cartoon brand; the biggest kids entry is the Turkish edition of an Arabic kids song channel at about 1.1M subscribers and about 33K average views, so Turkish is an under served language for animated kids songs, worth testing after the big languages.

Boom Buddies India (Hindi and English, 1.24M subscribers) drew about 15.8M views in 28 days to Nov 2026, more than the US main channel's 10.7M, yet vidIQ's modelled ad income was about 830 dollars against about 3,300 for the main channel, roughly a fifth of the money per view, so Hindi editions buy reach while English and European audiences pay the bills.

Kenyan kids brand Super Sema released a nursery rhyme album remade with Afrobeat rhythms, including a Swahili hello song, a Swahili Twinkle Twinkle and an African safari 'Bear Hunt', presenting them as heritage and bilingual learning, a model for Afrobeat flavoured Bro Bros versions aimed at Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana.

In a survey of 1,000 Filipino parents of 8 to 17 year olds (29 Oct to 2 Nov 2026) 34% said they use child specific apps such as YouTube Kids for safety and 97% want evidence based rules on children's social media, so Philippine families are open to supervised kids platforms and stricter rules may follow there too.

A University of the Philippines study of children aged 2 to 36 months found touchscreen video use of nearly two hours a day, with mothers choosing shows they see as educational and using that time to work or do chores, so English learning songs (colours, numbers, routines) suit Filipino parents, who already accept English content.

South Koreans spent about 113.6B minutes a month on YouTube in Jan to May 2026, over 20 times Netflix, while YouTube Music usage grew 186% since 2022 and now beats Melon and Spotify there, so for Korean families our songs should be on YouTube Music as well as on the main channel.

Pakistan's most subscribed YouTube list (Nov 2026) has few clear kids channels near the top; the main family entry is Peep Peep at 20th with 13.4M subscribers and 10.1B views, so Urdu kids songs look like an open space compared with the crowded Hindi kids market, though the data are thin.

An OpinionWay survey of 1,049 French parents of 3 to 10 year olds found screen exposure peaks in the winter holidays (96% of kids, average 1h51 a day in February versus 1 hour in term time, 16% over three hours), so holiday weeks are when French speaking families watch most.
leaves.src: OpinionWay for tonies via CB News, Feb 2026

leaves.t: In the same French survey 46% of parents said grandparents are more relaxed about screens and half leave screens on more in holidays for lack of time, so in holiday weeks the person pressing play is often a grandparent who searches simple words like song name plus 'comptine'.
leaves.src: OpinionWay for tonies via CB News, Feb 2026

leaves.t: 29% of French parents count watching cartoons together as family bonding time, which supports family singalong compilations in French for the Christmas and February holidays.
leaves.src: OpinionWay for tonies via CB News, Feb 2026

leaves.t: Kaboochi's French nursery rhyme channel (197K subscribers, 618 videos) gained no subscribers in the 28 days to 13 Nov 2026 and earns about 100K views a month, down from up to 255K a month in 2024, and its biggest hit is a Short, so small French dub channels stall and Shorts carry what reach they have.

A French expert commission (2024) advised no screens under 3, limited and accompanied screens from 3 to 6 and curbs on autoplay; French parents are primed to prefer calm, educational, co watched videos, so the French version of Bro Bros should lead with learning songs, not hype.

Parrot Analytics measured global audience demand for preschool titles up about 25% and school age titles up about 21% over the year to mid 2025, while TV demand overall fell, so kids content is one of the few growing categories worldwide.

India made Mighty Little Bheem reaches US demand at 76% of its Indian level, Pakistan 75% and the Philippines 74%, with Germany and Brazil above half, proof that a wordless or simple English kids brand created in India can be loved almost equally abroad.

A June 2026 survey of 367 Japanese primary school children found Minecraft (31.8%) and Roblox (12.7%, about eight times last year) are the most played games and HikakinGames is the favourite game YouTuber for the seventh year (29.6%), so block building and obby style challenge themes reach Japanese 6 to 12 year olds.

In a Shogakukan survey of 500 Japanese parents of 6 to 9 year olds, about 65% of children watch YouTube, most for 30 minutes to an hour a day, and the top channels are variety and Minecraft creators while kids educational channels rank 14th and below, so Japanese Bro Bros audio should aim at preschool families rather than school age kids.

Maasranga Kids, the children's channel of a Bangladeshi TV station and the only kids channel in Bangladesh's top 100 (vidIQ, 12 Nov 2026, 5.31M subscribers), grew from about 3.0B views in July 2025 to about 4.9B by November 2026 (roughly 120M views a month) by posting about 14 videos a week averaging 9 minutes, showing steady volume beats virality in this market.

A Swahili kids cartoon channel (Kids TV Africa, about 711K subscribers, 245M views from 872 videos) drew only about 28K views a day and gained no subscribers from 11 to 24 Oct 2026, so Swahili is a low priority dub for now compared with Spanish, Portuguese or Hindi.

Omo Berry, a Nigerian made 3D animated learning show with Black child characters and African rooted songs (launched on YouTube Feb 2021), had its biggest audiences in the US and UK ahead of Nigeria, showing that culturally specific kids songs travel through diaspora families in high ad rate countries; an Afrobeats flavoured Bro Bros song can do the same.

WildBrain runs six YouTube channels for The Fixies by language: English passed 3M subscribers and 3B views, Spanish 3M subscribers and 1.8B views, and an Arabic channel opened in 2024 already has 45M views, so Spanish deserves a full channel and Arabic is a fast growing extra.

Polish kids song channel Spiewajace Brzdace (2.61M subscribers, 5.1B views) got about 45.8M views and 10K new subscribers in the 28 days to 11 Nov 2026, and its biggest hits are short silly songs about one funny thing (a watermelon, a rooster, a pug, a little chicken), showing a mid sized language market of about 38M people can still give a local song channel tens of millions of views a month.

Moonbug's Arabic hub channel (909K subscribers) mixing dubbed Morphle, Blippi and other shows got only about 1.7M views and 1K subscribers in the 28 days to 14 Nov 2026, with a new upload at 3.65K views after three days, so a big brand's catch all dubbed channel underperforms in Arabic compared with focused single show channels like The Fixies Arabic.

For Bro Bros dubbing, the two data points together suggest one channel per language built around our own song catalogue with native sounding titles beats one mixed 'international' channel, and Polish is a realistic smaller market where a single funny food or animal song can carry the channel.
leaves.src: own synthesis of vidIQ data, Nov 2026

leaves.t: Germany's Hurra Kinderlieder (4.09M subscribers, 5.7B views) got about 58M views and 10K subscribers in the 28 days to 3 Nov 2026, and its biggest songs are about everyday moments and feelings: a haircut at the hairdresser (44M), an upside down world play song (32M), a tantrum told as a sudden thunderstorm (30M) and get well soon (28M).

A small Turkish kids song channel (Minnak, 201K subscribers, under 1M views a month) owes almost all its reach to one silly fruit character song, 'Watermelon Man' (8.6M views), and a watermelon song is also the top hit of Poland's biggest local song channel, so a goofy fruit character song is a cheap test that has travelled in two different markets.

In AIR's 2026 dataset a kids channel uploaded the same videos with Arabic, French and German audio tracks (16 Feb to 24 Mar 2026): Arabic drew 3.4M views, French 745K and German only 134K, yet German had the highest share of returning viewers (about 52% versus 47% and 42%) and the longest watch time for new viewers (4:30), so dub languages should be judged by how many viewers come back, not by raw views.

AIR's rule of thumb for a dubbed audio track: in the first 90 days most views come from new viewers, so judge it after about 4 months; if casual plus regular viewers are still under 20% of that track's views it is not working, 20 to 40% is building and above 40% is working (YouTube Analytics, Audience, watch behaviour, filtered by audio track).

Brazil's Portuguese kids song channel Cleo e Cuquin (6.42M subscribers, 5.36B views) has as its biggest hit a colourful train song (65M), followed by wheels on the bus, surprise eggs with numbers and colours, and a farm song, but its monthly views fell from about 135M in March 2026 to 44M in October, so vehicles, colours and farm topics travel to Brazil while even big local channels are losing ground this year.

The Arabic kids channel Tn Tn Baby (226K subscribers, 75M views) gets almost a third of all its views from one video, the 'without rhythm' (no instruments) version of its 'hello police, the thief ran away' song at 23.75M, about five times its normal version, which shows that many Muslim families look for vocals only kids songs; a voice only (or voice plus body percussion) edit of our best songs is a cheap extra upload for Arabic, Malay and Indonesian audiences.

Super Dido Kids Songs (474K subscribers, 261M views, about 4M views a month) has as its biggest Arabic hits a 'mama is coming home' song (39.8M), 'grandpa has a donkey' (23.8M), a fish in the sea song and a 'toot toot' train song, mostly as remixes, so family members, farm animals and trains are the safest themes for an Arabic Bro Bros version.

The police and runaway thief chase is the top theme of Tn Tn Baby (its five most viewed videos are all versions of it), echoing the 'who took the cookie' hook that works in Germany and on our own Reels, so a gentle chase or mystery story is a hook that crosses Arabic and European audiences alike.
leaves.src: own synthesis of vidIQ data, Nov 2026

leaves.t: LooLoo Kids' Spanish channel (La Alegría de Cantar, 1.57M subscribers, 664M views) gets its biggest views from a chicks and Lola the cow medley (362M) and then two 'who breaks the piñata?' party song compilations (79M and 43M), showing that the piñata party song is a big Latin American family favourite, useful for birthdays all year and for Mexico's posadas from 16 to 24 December.

Roy Morgan's survey of 1,129 Australian children aged 6 to 13 (Apr to Dec 2025, published Feb 2026) found 89% watch YouTube; for 6 to 9 year olds the top genres after gaming are animation (40%), animals (35%) and challenges (32%), girls lead on animals and music, and the under 16 ban does not cover YouTube Kids or logged out viewing, so animated animal songs with a little challenge are the best fit for young Australians.
YouTube's quality principles push high-quality made-for-kids videos up in recommendations and decide entry to the YouTube Kids app.
Six low-quality types to avoid: heavily promotional, negative behaviour, fake-educational, hard to follow/mass-produced, sensational or keyword-stuffed, odd use of familiar characters.
Red flags: flashing lights, loud or sudden sounds, chaotic camera moves, rushed storytelling, mean characters even as jokes.
YouTube is cracking down on low-effort AI 'slop' for kids; originality and consistent quality matter more in 2026.
Getting into the YouTube Kids app is done through review (often via an official YouTube partner), not by applying directly.

There is no public banned word list, but words in six risk clusters (fear, conflict, medical, danger, emotional overload like 'shocking', adult themes like 'crush') lower kids recommendations and ads.

Kids and teens has the lowest median RPM of 13 niches, about 0.33 USD per 1,000 views versus about 2.30 overall (300 channels, May 2025 to May 2026), so kids channels win on volume and long watch sessions.

YouTube requires disclosing AI generated music (its detector does not scan soundtracks, so it is on us); clearly animated or unreal visuals need no label, and for animated work the label sits in the expanded description and does not cut reach.
Since 27 May 2026 YouTube auto applies AI labels to undeclared photorealistic AI; repeated failure to disclose can lead to removal or Partner Program suspension.

YouTube's Jul 2026 inauthentic content update names three non monetisable types: generic or repetitive template series with the same situations and outcomes, unsatisfying shock or stitched AI clips, and AI 'experts' on sensitive topics; a clear original creative spin keeps AI assisted work safe.

The FTC's amended COPPA Rule compliance date was 22 Apr 2026: every video needs an audience setting, YouTube's classifier can mark videos as for kids (appeal only), and Disney paid 10M USD partly for labelling whole channels instead of each video.
Made for kids channels are excluded from YouTube Shopping affiliates and lose personalised ads, comments and notifications, so revenue depends on views and watch time volume.

Suno songs can only be monetised if made on a paid plan (Pro or Premier) at the time of creation; fully AI songs get no copyright, so adding our own written lyrics and arrangement edits protects the human parts. Keep receipts and creation dates per song.
Suno settled with Warner Music and is moving to licensed models with monthly download caps; current v5 models will be phased out, so back up the full song catalogue now.

YouTube Kids entry runs through automated filters that read thumbnails, titles and the video itself, plus human spot checks and parent reports; paid placements, purchase pushing and toy packaging videos are excluded.
leaves.src: Team YouTube FAQ via PPC Land, Apr 2026

leaves.t: YouTube's Mar 2026 Dublin summit treats kids and teens as separate audiences and signals that YouTube Kids will favour less overstimulating, authentic, human made content over mindless AI output.

Songs released as YouTube Music Art Tracks through a distributor earn much more per 1,000 streams than Content ID claims (UK 18.87 USD, Germany 14.05, US 11.22), a second income stream for our Suno songs made on the paid plan.

YouTube's five high quality traits for kids content are kindness and healthy habits, curiosity and learning, creativity and imaginative play, life skills with clear lessons, and diverse people and places; videos with them are promoted in recommendations.
Quality is judged at two levels: a single low quality video gets limited or no ads, while a channel that focuses on low quality content can be suspended from the Partner Program.
'Deceptively educational' is a named low quality type: a title or thumbnail that promises learning must deliver accurate learning in the video, so 'learn colours' songs must really teach colours.
'Hard to follow' storylines count as low quality, so each song should tell one clear, simple story from start to finish.

Even large kids channels (PlayToys, 8M subs) can be missing from the YouTube Kids app; after a partner escalated to YouTube's review team on 20 May, the Kids team approved them by 18 Jun, after which they became searchable and appeared as suggestions.

YouTube Kids filtering (Team YouTube FAQ, 1 Apr 2026) works in layers: automated filters read thumbnails, titles and the video itself, human reviewers spot check and refine the filters, and parent flags are reviewed around the clock and removed for everyone if upheld.

YouTube Kids excludes paid product placements, videos that push purchases, packaging and unboxing focused videos and excessive accumulation or consumption of products, so our songs should never feature branded toys or buying.
YouTube renamed the Partner Program's 'repetitious content' rule to 'mass produced content' on 15 Jul 2025; with 14 songs a week we must keep each song clearly different in story, setting and moves.
Community Guidelines strikes: a first violation is usually a warning that expires after 90 days with policy training; three strikes within 90 days can terminate the channel.
YouTube Kids added over 100 Sesame Street episodes in Jan 2026, so trusted educational brands are now direct competitors on the YouTube Kids learning shelf.
94% of teachers worldwide use YouTube in class (YouTube, Jan 2026), so classroom friendly songs (brain breaks, routines, counting) can earn repeat plays on school screens.

YouTube Music started labelling songs 'created primarily using generative AI' on 14 Oct 2026 (composition and vocals both AI) using partner data and its own detection, with the main YouTube app to follow; per YouTube's May 2026 policy a label alone does not change recommendations or monetisation.

Unlike YouTube, Spotify keeps AI badged artist profiles out of recommendations by default and Deezer removes AI detected tracks from algorithmic and editorial playlists, so AI made songs earn mostly on YouTube, not audio stores.
Suno songs are commercially usable (YouTube monetisation, distribution) only if made while on a paid Pro or Premier plan; free tier songs never convert, and the status stays after cancelling.

After the Nov 2025 Warner Music deal, Suno is moving to licensed models and capping downloads (about 20 a month on Pro, 60 on Premier), so we should download and back up every final song and stem as we make it.
The EU AI Act's transparency duties (Article 50) applied from 2 Aug 2026, with fines up to 15M EUR or 3% of turnover, adding another reason to disclose AI music clearly in descriptions.

YouTube confirmed (10 Aug 2026) that from 1 Feb 2027 new Partner Program applicants need 1,000 subscribers plus 8,000 public watch hours in 365 days, or 20M Shorts views in 90 days (double today); members admitted before then are grandfathered, so qualifying before February matters.

From 1 Feb 2027 Shorts pool revenue becomes a rolling test: a channel needs 10M qualified Shorts views in each rolling 90 days or its Shorts pool pay pauses that month; long form ads are unaffected, and partners must accept new modules by 31 Jan 2027.
A channel must also stay active to keep YPP from 2027: 1,000 watch hours in 365 days, 1M Shorts views in 90 days, or at least two long videos or five Shorts every 90 days.

The UK announced (15 Jun 2026) an under 16 social media ban modelled on Australia's (live since 10 Dec 2025), naming YouTube among covered platforms but leaving YouTube Kids outside it; rules are due by end 2026 and should apply from spring 2027.

YouTube Kids is a filtered copy of YouTube: automated filters check each video's thumbnail, title and content and any one can block it, with humans only spot checking; videos built around product packaging, urging kids to buy, paid placements or excessive consumption are kept out, so Bro Bros songs should never show branded toys or 'get yours' moments.

Since May 2026 YouTube shows a prominent AI label (under the player, or over a Short) only for photorealistic AI; for animated or stylised content like ours the disclosure appears only in the expanded description, and YouTube says a disclosure label does not change recommendations or monetisation, so ticking the AI box costs us nothing.

In AIR's 300 channel study (May 2025 to May 2026) kids and teens content was monetised on only about 32% of playbacks, the lowest of 13 niches, because made for kids videos cannot carry personalised ads, but it gets about a 22% lift in Q4; volume and reach, not rate per view, drive kids channel income.

On 15 Oct 2026 YouTube announced an invite only Monthly Shorts Bonus pilot for Partner Program creators in the US, UK, Germany, Brazil, Japan and South Korea; India is not in the first wave, another reason to build US and UK viewers.
From 26 Oct 2026 YouTube tests a 20 USD payout threshold (down from 100) for a random group of creators in the US, India and Indonesia, so small new channels may get first earnings sooner.

Since 29 Oct 2026 YouTube tests offering some channels with spam policy violations a 30 day cleanup lock (edit or delete videos, or wipe all videos but keep subscribers and handle) instead of termination; repetitive or templated uploads remain the main risk for high volume channels like ours.

Seasonal ad money: YouTube RPM runs about 0.5 times its spring baseline in January and about 1.8 to 2.5 times in December, and the two weeks before 25 Dec have the most competitive ad auctions, so our best holiday compilations should be live by the first days of December.

Precisify (Feb 2026): 80% of parents say their child asked for something seen in a YouTube ad while co viewing and 50% bought because of YouTube ads, which is why advertisers pay for kids views; our own videos must still never urge purchases, or they drop out of YouTube Kids.

Under COPPA and GDPR K, kids content must never ask children to send names, photos, videos or contest entries, nor use sign up links or tracking pixels, and that applies off YouTube too, so our Instagram captions should address parents and never invite kids to submit anything.

Since Aug 2025 YouTube's AI age estimation can treat signed in viewers it infers are minors as minors even on videos not marked made for kids, changing what is recommended and how ads run; COPPA 2.0 (protections to age 16) is still only proposed in the US.

In January 2026 YouTube terminated 16 mass produced AI channels with 35M subscribers and 4.7B lifetime views under its inauthentic content policy; enforcement judges a pattern across a channel's recent uploads (about the last 30), so one batch of templated songs can cut monetisation on every video.

After that purge faceless channels that never used AI also report demonetisation, while niche educational channels held up better; YouTube says AI labelled videos are not penalised and only mass produced, templated content without human creative input is targeted, so visible human craft (our own lyrics, stories, edits) is the protection.

A Kapwing test found about 21% of the first 500 videos recommended to a new account were AI slop, a New York Times check found over 40% of Shorts recommended after popular preschool videos were AI made, and 230 experts asked YouTube in April 2026 to ban AI content from YouTube Kids, so stricter AI rules for kids are likely.

India's DPDP rules define a child as anyone under 18, require verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data and ban tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads aimed at children, with fines up to 200 crore rupees; our Indian audience reach must stay on platform made for kids settings, never our own data collection.

YouTube's more prominent AI labels (May 2026) are not shown on YouTube Kids at all, which runs under separate policies, and animated AI videos on main YouTube only get a label tucked in the description; advocacy groups (Fairplay) now ask YouTube to stop recommending AI made for kids videos, so expect future limits aimed at animated AI kids content.

Neal Mohan's 2026 letter said YouTube would adapt its anti spam and anti clickbait systems to spot and demote low effort AI videos and strictly enforce synthetic media labels, so the defence for an AI assisted channel is clear human authorship and variety, not hiding AI use.

Since 10 Dec 2025 Australian under 16s are signed out of YouTube: they can still watch, but lose subscriptions, playlists, likes and wellbeing defaults, and parents lose supervised accounts; YouTube Kids is not affected, so in Australia (and later the UK and other copycat bans) the Kids app and signed out recommendations carry family viewing.

The EU's Digital Services Act guidelines on minors (Jul 2025) ask every platform kids may use to offer feeds children can reset and understand, private defaults, no overuse features like streaks or endless scroll, and clearly labelled child suitable ads; countdown timers and buy now prompts aimed at kids are discouraged, so our songs must never push kids to buy or demand things.

2026 estimates put Shorts RPM at about 0.10 to 0.32 USD per 1,000 views in the US and 0.09 to 0.19 in Australia, the UK, Germany and Canada, against 0.01 to 0.03 in India, Indonesia and the Philippines, so Shorts views from high income English markets earn about ten times more.

In Jul 2026 YouTube brought supervised kid accounts to the Middle East, North Africa and Turkiye, with three content levels, a Shorts timer that can switch Shorts off and, for every under 18, no personalised ads and autoplay off by default, so Arabic and Turkish families now get the same controls as the US and Europe.

The UK's first national screen guidance for under 5s (27 Mar 2026) says under 2s should use screens only for shared bonding activities, 2 to 5s at most an hour a day and none at meals or in the hour before bed, with slow paced content and no fast social media style videos; watching together is better than solo use.

Suno's 2026 rights terms (after its Nov 2025 Warner settlement): songs made on a free account can never be used commercially, and subscribing later gives no retroactive licence; songs made while subscribed carry commercial rights for streaming, downloads and sync with no revenue share, but users are no longer treated as owners of the songs.

Suno v6 (9 Sep 2026) runs on models co developed with Warner Music, BMG and Believe and all older models are being retired; free songs can no longer be downloaded and paid plans have monthly download limits (extra downloads cost more), so 14 songs a week plus remixes must fit our plan's download allowance.

A German court ruled in 2026, in a case brought by the collecting society GEMA, that Suno breached copyright, and Universal is not part of Suno's licensing deals, so prompts and lyrics must never name real artists or imitate known songs, keeping our catalogue clean if rules tighten.

Since mid 2025 Instagram treats adult managed accounts that mainly feature children with strict message settings, Hidden Words comment filtering, and no recommendations to or from potentially suspicious adults (also harder to find in Search); Meta has not said whether animated child characters count, so a small cut in odd adult reach is possible but parents still see us.

Instagram teen accounts default to a 13+ content level modelled on film ratings (US, UK, Australia and Canada since Oct 2025, India since 9 Apr 2026), with an even stricter Limited Content option; accounts flagged for age inappropriate posts lose teen followers and reach, so clean, gentle songs keep our Reels open to older siblings.

Because children under 13 cannot hold Instagram accounts, our Instagram audience is parents, carers and teens; captions and Reels should be written to parents (what the song helps with, a question for them) rather than to the child.

vidIQ models only about 10K USD of ad income for Tunes Kids' roughly 30M monthly Arabic views, a sign that Arabic made for kids views earn far less per view than English ones, so Arabic tracks are mainly for reach and brand growth.

YouTube Help lists what made for kids videos lose on their watch pages: autoplay on Home, cards and end screens, the video watermark (subscribe button), memberships, comments, donate and Super Chat, live chat, merch and tickets, notifications, personalised ads, Miniplayer playback, and save to playlist or Watch Later.

Made for kids channels also cannot use community posts, so channel news (new song days, holiday mixes) can only reach parents through Instagram, video titles and the channel banner, not YouTube posts.

Ads shown in YouTube Kids need pre approval from YouTube's policy team and food and drink, beauty and fitness, dating and political ads are barred, so YouTube Kids views earn less per view than main YouTube and should be judged by reach, not income.

Since 21 Oct 2026 YouTube automatically pauses features on channels that look hacked while it reviews them, usually within 24 hours and without touching monetisation, and since 29 Oct some channels facing spam termination get a 30 day lock to fix videos or appeal instead of instant removal.

Vietnam's National Assembly debated in 2026 restricting minors' use of some social apps and stricter identity checks for under 16s, citing Australia's ban (Dec 2025) and similar steps in Indonesia and France since Mar 2026; nothing is law yet, but signed out family viewing on TV and YouTube Kids is where Southeast Asian kids markets are heading.
Shorts that use licensed music from YouTube's library are capped at 60 seconds, but our own original Suno songs are not, though 25 to 40 seconds remains the performance sweet spot.

More than 200 child advocacy groups and child development experts (2026) asked YouTube to ban AI generated videos from the YouTube Kids app and give parents tools to limit AI content on main YouTube; for an AI assisted channel like ours, proof of human craft (original songs, designed characters, real story and learning goals) is the best protection if rules tighten.

YouTube's synthetic content disclosure rule exempts clearly unrealistic animation, so our 3D cartoons do not need an 'altered or synthetic' label, while anything that looks realistic (photoreal people, fake real world footage) would; scripts and captions written with AI also need no disclosure.

A Los Angeles jury found Google and Meta negligent in designing YouTube and Instagram and failing to warn users (25 Mar 2026, 6M USD, appeal planned), a bellwether for thousands of child harm cases with more trials due in 2026, so expect further kid safeguards such as less autoplay and scrolling that reduce passive binge views.

With pressure on attention grabbing design for kids, songs that end calmly, invite a real world action (go brush your teeth, time for bed) and avoid endless cliffhangers fit where regulators and parents are pushing YouTube, and are less likely to be hit by future limits.

The same guide says kids content runs at roughly half the normal CPM (made for kids ads are not personalised) and that Q4 and Ramadan bring 30 to 50% RPM spikes in the Middle East, so Arabic songs should be ready before Ramadan 2027 (about mid February).

AIR's 274 channel RPM study (Sep 2026) found Kids and Teens Shorts had a 45.7% monetised playback rate against only 12.1% for long form because of made for kids ad limits, about 2,156 Shorts views equal 1,000 long views for large kids channels, and Shorts made 41% of revenue for big kids channels posting 21+ Shorts a month.

In the same study a kids channel's long form RPM fell about 26% in months when it posted Shorts, and Shorts RPM by viewer country was 0.33 USD in the US against about 0.16 to 0.19 in Australia, the UK, Canada and Germany (correlational, vendor data).

Since March 2026 YouTube has been testing a mobile pop up that asks viewers to rate on a five point scale whether a video feels like AI slop, and it now labels AI made videos automatically from C2PA metadata and SynthID watermarks rather than relying only on creator disclosure, so visible human craft (story, gags, varied scenes) protects AI assisted songs like ours.

A 7.55M subscriber kids channel cut long uploads from 21 to 11 and raised Shorts from 10 to 23 in Q4 2025 against Q3, moved to 4K with TV safe text, higher contrast colours and audio mixed for TV speakers, and revenue grew about 34% on roughly 6% more views.

FluxNote's unsourced 2026 seasonal model puts November RPM around 3 times January and December about 3.6 to 5 times January, with the two weeks before 25 December the most competitive ad auctions of the year, so our best Christmas songs should be live by late November.

The New York Times' Feb 2026 test found the AI slop served to toddlers had warped faces, garbled text, no repetition, no story and no clip longer than 30 seconds; YouTube removed five cited channels from the Partner Program and YouTube Kids, so Bro Bros Shorts should always show a repeated hook and a tiny beginning, middle and end.

YouTube divides Shorts pool money with music rights holders by the number of licensed tracks used (one track takes roughly half of that Short's share), so Bro Bros Shorts built only on our own original songs keep the full creator share, a quiet money advantage over channels using library music.

Since March 2026 videos that show young subjects in distress with shocking imagery lose ad eligibility, so no crying or scared baby faces in Bro Bros thumbnails or opening frames, even for 'feelings' songs; show the happy ending face instead.

YouTube Premium Lite (no ads on most videos) is expanding to all Premium countries but keeps ads on music content and excludes YouTube Music, so song videos still earn ad money from Lite subscribers where other videos do not.
Content ID also scans multi language audio tracks, and YouTube skips auto dubbing on any video with a copyright claim, one more reason every Bro Bros track and dub uses only our own Suno music.

Sydney the Song Cat, a hand drawn kids song channel made over four years, was demonetised as 'inauthentic content' in spring 2026 even with a clean record, because it reused rigs and backgrounds; appeals with storyboards and voice recordings got template replies and it had to wait for a July re apply window.

In February 2026, shortly after YouTube removed big AI slop channels, popular kaiju and dinosaur animation channels also lost monetisation with no clear guidance, so reused 3D assets plus repetitive templates can be read as mass produced even when the work is original.

To protect monetisation every Bro Bros song should leave a visible human trail: an original story idea per video, varied scenes and choreography, real lyric changes rather than template swaps, and saved making of material (Suno prompts, Meshy prompts, Blender files, storyboards) to attach to any appeal.

The FTC's amended COPPA Rule (in force June 2025) had a compliance date of 22 April 2026, and YouTube used that date to require every creator, even non kids ones, to set the audience per channel or per video; FTC civil penalties reach about 53K USD per violation.

Once YouTube's systems apply a made for kids label the creator cannot change it, only appeal in Studio, and made for kids channels are excluded from the YouTube Shopping affiliate programme, so merchandise links must live off YouTube (website, Instagram).

Meta announced in June 2026 that its 13+ content setting for teen accounts (no suggestive, graphic, strong language, risky stunt or alcohol content in Explore, Reels and search) goes global across Instagram, Facebook and Messenger after India got it in April; clean family songs are not affected, but risky stunt jokes would be.
The Elf on the Shelf is a trademarked character and brand, so Bro Bros must design its own helper elf (different name, look and story) and never use that name or look in titles, tags or thumbnails.

Much Brazilian funk and phonk carries explicit lyrics and adult dance styles, so Bro Bros borrows only the rhythm (a bouncy tamborzao style drum pattern) in its own Suno songs, never the trending tracks or their moves.

CIMM notes that kids content earns lower CPMs, that ad tech often cannot work in COPPA compliant settings so children's videos are left out of programmatic buying, and that advertisers rarely buy YouTube made for kids inventory, which is why kids channel RPMs stay low and scale matters.

Since May 2026 YouTube auto detects and labels undisclosed photorealistic AI video, placing the label under the player on long videos and as an overlay on Shorts, but animated or stylised content (including animated AI music videos) only carries a disclosure in the expanded description.

YouTube says an AI disclosure label does not change recommendations or monetisation eligibility, and creators can correct a wrong label in Studio except for permanent labels on videos made with YouTube's own AI tools or carrying C2PA fully AI metadata.

Brazil's ECA Digital (child and teen online safety statute) has been fully in force since 17 Mar 2026 for services likely to be used by minors, including streaming and social platforms and foreign providers: it bans ad profiling of minors and compulsive design features and requires protective defaults and guardian linked accounts under 16.

Brazil's regulator scheduled administrative sanctions under ECA Digital from November 2026 and formal enforcement from January 2027, with fines up to 10% of Brazilian revenue; its decree on child influencers needs court approval to monetise real children, which does not touch an animated channel like ours.

Because laws in Brazil, the EU and the UK now target designs that encourage compulsive use, Bro Bros should avoid manipulative hooks aimed at kids (fake countdowns to keep watching, 'don't stop now' prompts) and keep endings that invite a calm goodbye.
leaves.src: Mayer Brown and earlier rules leaves, 2026

leaves.t: The Nutcracker story and Tchaikovsky's music are public domain, but specific film or ballet company designs are not, so Bro Bros can use a toy soldier and music box idea with our own designs and our own newly written melody rather than any recording.

Creator data compiled in 2026 puts long form RPM highest in Australia (about 10 to 12 USD per 1,000 views), the US (9 to 11), Canada (8 to 10) and New Zealand (8 to 9), and lowest in Bangladesh, Pakistan and the Philippines (about 0.2 to 0.5) and Vietnam (0.3 to 0.7).
The same compilation puts the kids and animation niche at about 1 to 4 USD RPM (median about 2.5) for US heavy long form audiences, with roughly a 1.5 times multiplier in Q4.

For US facing channels December RPM averages about 74% above January lows, while lower paying markets see only about a 25 to 30% Q4 lift, so our December holiday songs aimed at the US, UK, Canada and Australia are the year's best earning uploads and January needs cheaper, evergreen production.

Trends that put a real child's photo into a frame (for example Santa's nice list) are popular with parents, but Bro Bros must never ask viewers to send children's photos or names, keeping to made for kids privacy rules.

YouTube renamed 'repetitious content' to 'inauthentic content' in July 2025, and creator guides report its checks look for upload cadence high for the channel's age, audio that clusters tightly from the same AI tool and presets, near identical thumbnails, formulaic titles and low watch time, so at 14 songs a week Bro Bros must vary Suno style prompts, instruments and tempos song to song.

Reused content enforcement on AI audio is reported to hit three patterns: the same AI beat under different thumbnails, re uploads of others' AI tracks, and long compilations that loop one short segment with small changes, so our Friday compilations must be made of distinct full songs, never one song looped.

AI music is not banned from monetisation: creator guides say disclosure through the 'Altered or synthetic content' setting does not by itself disqualify a video, while raw unedited AI dumps and voice clones of real artists are what gets demonetised; checking each track with YouTube Studio's copyright check before publishing and regenerating any claimed track is advised because AI models can echo songs from their training data.

Under Indonesia's PP Tunas child protection regulation, Google committed in a 17 Apr 2026 letter to a minimum YouTube account age of 16 there, began removing under 16 accounts gradually and said it would stop ads targeted at children, after the ministry reprimanded YouTube on 10 Apr and listed it among eight 'high risk' platforms.

Because Indonesian children can no longer hold their own YouTube accounts, our Indonesian audience will mostly arrive through parents' accounts, signed out viewing or family devices, so Indonesian titles, descriptions and dubbed tracks should speak to parents' searches (lagu anak, lagu tidur) rather than to kids typing.

As of Aug 2026 COPPA 2.0 had passed the US Senate unanimously and the KIDS Act passed the House (29 Jun 2026), but neither was law, and KOSA was still awaiting a committee markup, so the amended COPPA Rule (compliance from 22 Apr 2026) remains the binding US standard for our videos.

Four US states have app store accountability acts (Texas in force after a 4 Jun 2026 court stay, Alabama from 1 Jan 2027), 26 states have age verification laws and California may now require age estimation, so more platforms will know a viewer is a child and route them to kid settings, which rewards correctly marked made for kids videos.

The EU Kids Act, proposed on 17 Sep 2026 and still needing Parliament and Council approval, would ban personal accounts for under 13s on platforms including YouTube, allow parent set 'mini accounts' for ages 13 to 15 with up to one hour a day, and end self declared birthdates.

The same proposal would switch off engagement based recommendations for minors by default, ban behaviour profiled feeds for them and prohibit endless autoplay and infinite scrolling, so in Europe our growth would lean on search, subscriptions, playlists and parents' own feeds rather than kid personalised recommendations.

Australia's eSafety evaluation (data from March 2026) found the share of under 16s with a social media account fell only from 52.4% to 42.1% after the ban, mostly because age checks were weak, and most families said they were not yet affected.

AIR's September 2026 study puts Shorts RPM by audience country at about $0.33 for the US, $0.19 Australia and about $0.16 to $0.17 for the UK, Canada and Germany, so a million Shorts views earn about $300 from a US heavy audience but only $150 to $250 from a mixed global one.

The same study found channels with audiences mainly in Nigeria, Pakistan or the Philippines see long form CPMs of only $0.20 to $1.50, against $8 to $20 for European, American or Australian audiences, so dubs for lower paying markets grow reach while English keeps the revenue.

YouTube's Q3 2026 ad revenue was about $11.2B, up 9.2% year on year, the slowest growth of 2026 (11% in Q1, 13% in Q2), so ad rates are not rising fast and Bro Bros revenue growth has to come mostly from more watch time, especially long TV views.

Nielsen put YouTube at a record 15.8% of all US TV viewing in August 2026, and viewers watch about 2B hours of Shorts a month on TV screens, which keeps living room friendly long compilations the most valuable format for a kids song channel.

Premium connected TV CPMs reportedly jumped from about $34 to $43 during the US midterm political ad season (to early Nov 2026), and that demand ends after election day, so late November and December prices will depend on holiday retail advertisers rather than politics.

Mexico's online child safety decree took effect on 14 Oct 2026 and requires covered platforms (social networks, games, app stores) to verify users' ages without relying only on self declared age, with compliance reports due 13 Nov 2026, so Mexican kids may increasingly watch through parent or supervised accounts.

New York's final SAFE for Kids Act rules (released 28 Jul 2026, in force 25 Jan 2027) forbid giving minors an algorithmic 'addictive' feed without age assurance or verified parental consent and ban notifications to minors between midnight and 6 AM, while still letting minors see content without the feed, so search, playlists and subscriptions matter more for reaching older kids.

The Q4 ad boost is smaller for kids content: AIR data summarised by Gyre (Nov 2026) shows median RPM rising about 22% in Q4 for kids and teens versus about 60% for business and finance and 39% for food, because made for kids videos only carry contextual ads.

Across niches, regular video RPM peaked in November 2025 (median 2.35 USD, 2.12 in December, 1.56 in January) while live stream RPM peaked a month later in December (5.47 USD versus 2.31 in January), so a Bro Bros 24/7 holiday stream started before Black Friday (27 Nov 2026) catches the best paying weeks.

For an unattended 24/7 stream YouTube serves no mid roll ads in Manual mode, so mid rolls must be set to Automatic, and the stream must use only music we own (Content ID claims interrupt it) and real moving content rather than a still image or slideshow, which can break monetisation rules.

Malaysia began enforcing a ban on social media accounts for under 16s on 1 Jun 2026 for platforms with at least 8M users, naming YouTube along with Facebook, Instagram and TikTok; existing accounts are age checked over six months, so Malaysian kids will mostly watch Bro Bros signed out or through parents' and supervised accounts, not their own.

Ofcom found 73% of UK 11 to 17 year olds met harmful content in a four week window (36% of them on YouTube) and asked platforms for safer feeds, but YouTube declined major recommendation changes (May 2026), so UK made for kids discovery rules are unchanged for now; fines can reach 10% of global revenue if Ofcom acts.

India's DPDP Rules (notified Nov 2025) roll out in stages: consent manager registration from Nov 2026 and most other duties by May 2027, with Rule 10 letting platforms check parental consent through age or identity tokens from authorised entities such as DigiLocker, so Indian children's accounts and comments will narrow further next year.

Since late May 2026 YouTube shows AI labels as an overlay on Shorts and directly under the player on long videos, but non realistic content such as animation and fantasy is excluded from mandatory disclosure, so our stylised 3D cartoon songs do not need the realistic AI label, while any photoreal scene or voice clone of a real person would.

The House passed KIDS Act (H.R. 7757, 29 Jun 2026) bundles 14 proposals: it would extend children's privacy protection to teens, ban targeted ads to minors, make the most protective settings the default and restrict autoplay, push notifications and infinite scroll for minors; if it became law, autoplay chains would weaken and each Bro Bros video would need to earn its own click from Home and Search.

The KIDS Act drops KOSA's duty of care, and Senate KOSA sponsor Richard Blumenthal called the House version dead in the Senate, so no new US federal kids online law is likely before 2027 and the current COPPA rules remain the ones we follow.

Texas's App Store Accountability Act has been enforceable since 28 May 2026 while its appeal runs (the Fifth Circuit let it stand on 5 Jun), while Utah's deadline moved to 6 May 2027 and Louisiana's to 1 Jul 2027; app stores pass apps age bands (under 13, 13 to 15, 16 to 17, 18+) and parental consent signals, so more US children will reach YouTube through supervised and kids profiles.

Shorts ad pay by viewer country (AIR, per 1,000 views): US about 0.33 USD, UK 0.17, Germany 0.16, France 0.10, Brazil 0.045, Indonesia 0.012 and India 0.008, so a Short watched in the US earns about 40 times one watched in India, which is why English Shorts that reach US and UK homes matter for income.

In the Shorts revenue pool, using one licensed track from YouTube's music partners sends 50% of that Short's allocation to music rights holders and two tracks send 67%, before the creator's 45% share; our Shorts use only our own original songs, so none of our allocation is split off for music.

Since 31 Mar 2025 YouTube counts every Short start as a view but still pays on 'engaged views', so Shorts view counts look bigger than what is paid and RPM figures before and after that date are not comparable.

YouTube is piloting a monthly Shorts consistency bonus (reported 16 to 23 Oct 2026): invite only Partner Program creators in the US, UK, Germany, Brazil, Japan and South Korea get a base payment for hitting a set number of public Shorts a month plus a bonus tied to valid engaged Shorts views; India is not in the pilot and made for kids eligibility is not stated.

The FTC's 10M USD COPPA settlement with Disney (Sep 2025) was over audience labels set per channel instead of per video: child directed videos sitting on 'not made for kids' channels got targeted ads and data collection, so Bro Bros must set 'made for kids' on every single upload, including Shorts and compilations, not rely on the channel default.

Disney's settlement also requires a standing review programme for each video's audience label, and the FTC noted YouTube had already flipped 300+ Disney videos to made for kids in 2020; a simple upload checklist line ('audience: made for kids, checked') is our cheap version of that review.

An FTC policy statement (25 Feb 2026) promises no COPPA action over data collected only to check a user's age on general or mixed audience services, but services aimed mainly at children get no such relief and must treat every viewer as a child, which is why a kids channel can never collect names, photos or entries.

Since October 2026 payments YouTube is testing a 20 USD AdSense payout minimum instead of 100 USD for randomly chosen Partner Program members in the US, India and Indonesia; creators can raise it in AdSense and eligibility for the Partner Program does not change.

YouTube Music began labelling songs as 'Fully Gen AI' or 'Partly Gen AI' on 14 Oct 2026, using what music partners declare at delivery plus YouTube's own detection, and the label will spread to the main YouTube app; a track made from a text prompt in an AI generator counts as Fully Gen AI, so our Suno songs should be declared honestly when distributed.

YouTube has not said whether AI music labels change recommendations or royalties; for videos it said in May 2026 that a disclosure label alone does not change reach or monetisation, so adding our own sung or played layers on top of Suno tracks is a quality choice, not a ranking trick.

Moonbug's partner, UCLA's Center for Scholars and Storytellers, rates content on four principles: real life moments, positive relationships, learning through play and authentically inclusive stories; Moonbug's older content scored 1 out of 2 on its rubric, so building these four into each Bro Bros song gives a simple quality check parents trust.

The European Commission proposed the Digital Fairness Act on 11 Nov 2026: it bans manipulative dark patterns, restricts personalised ads and prices aimed at minors, requires clear influencer marketing disclosure, lets users switch off addictive features and allows fines up to 6% of worldwide turnover; it still needs Parliament and Council approval.

Under the EU Digital Fairness Act proposal non EU companies selling to EU consumers would need an EU legal representative and the Commission could investigate large cross border cases directly, which matters for Bro Bros only if we later sell apps, games or merch with in app coins to European families.

Ofcom found 73% of UK 11 to 17 year olds met harmful content in a four week window (36% of those on YouTube) and asked platforms for safer feeds in March 2026; Snap, Meta and Roblox committed to new protections, but YouTube declined a major feed overhaul, saying its systems already protect children.

Since Brazil's ECA Digital took effect on 17 Mar 2026, YouTube requires channels run by under 16s in Brazil to be linked to a supervising parent or guardian or lose access, and uses machine learning age estimation from watch, search and like signals to restrict teen profiles; Bro Bros has adult owners and animated characters, so it is not affected, but family creator rivals there are.

A draft ECA Digital decree reported in Brazil would require platforms to see a court authorisation before monetising or boosting content made by child creators, a sign that real kid performers are getting harder to use commercially, which favours animated characters like ours.

OutlierKit's risk scale for YouTube's inauthentic content rules (updated Oct 2026): fully automated channels and template clones are high risk, daily uploads with little variation and unreviewed AI pipelines are medium risk, and AI assisted work with human creative direction is low risk, so each Bro Bros song needs visibly new story, setting or choreography, not just a new title.

Creators can block AI remixing of their Shorts in YouTube Studio under 'Shorts remixing', but that also turns off normal remixes (Cut, Green Screen, Collab); since kids remixes of our dance Shorts can spread the Bros, we should keep remixing on and watch for misuse of our characters.

YouTube said in April 2026 that the YouTube Kids app limits AI generated content to a small set of high quality channels and lets parents block any channel, so Bro Bros must look clearly crafted (consistent characters, original songs, real story) to be one of the AI assisted channels allowed into the app.

Fairplay's 1 Apr 2026 open letter to YouTube, signed by 135 organisations and about 100 experts, asks YouTube to label all AI video, ban it from YouTube Kids, stop recommending it to under 18s and give parents an off switch; if any of this is adopted, AI assisted kids channels without visible human craft lose reach first.

YouTube's disclosure rule still covers only realistic synthetic media: clearly unrealistic content such as animation does not need the altered or synthetic label, so our stylised 3D cartoons need no AI label, though YouTube says it is building separate labels for YouTube Kids.
leaves.src: The Star / Fairplay, Apr and May 2026

leaves.t: Fairplay called YouTube's May 2026 AI label pledge lip service because animated AI videos only get a label tucked in the description and children who cannot read cannot use labels; its next ask is fewer made for kids AI videos in recommendations, so quality signals (watch time, likes, low skip rate) are our protection.

Across 300 channels, the median all format RPM peaked in November (2.35 USD), dipped in December (2.12) and fell to 1.56 in January, and kids and teens RPM rose about 22% in Q4, so the most valuable upload weeks of the year are right now, before Black Friday (27 Nov 2026).
